bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives means financial products which provide a financial return based on price movements of Securities, including exchange traded options or options granted by third parties, and includes financial products (including equity swaps, caps and collars and other hedging arrangements) which have the effect of limiting exposure to risks associated with such price movements. ... Designated Persons must not trade in Brambles Derivatives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written put and call is an 'option granted by a third party' and a 'collar', so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited by name for all Designated Persons regardless of vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not grant a Security Interest over any Brambles Securities they hold. ... Security Interest means a pledge, lien, charge, mortgage or other encumbrance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright; the ban is not limited to margin loans and has no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Designated Person were to take out a margin loan and the security for that loan included Brambles Securities, the lender may be able to sell or otherwise Deal in those Securities. This would be so notwithstanding that, at the relevant time, there may be a Closed Period or the Designated Person may be in possession of price sensitive information ... This could cause the Designated Person to be in breach of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy treats a lender's enforcement sale as the Designated Person's own breach, so lender enforcement rights cannot be relied on even if a security interest were somehow permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may still acquire Brambles Securities through a margin or other investment loan if Brambles Securities are not used as security for that loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only a loan with no security over Brambles Securities is open, which removes the secured-loan element that defines a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their nominee, including an investment manager managing funds on their behalf; a trust of which they, any member of their family, or any family controlled company, are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which they or their family control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar or secured loan through a family trust, nominee or controlled company remains within the derivatives and Security Interest bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval can be given or refused at Brambles' discretion without giving reasons. A refusal to approve a request to Deal in Brambles Securities is final and binding ... The Designated Person will be notified if the clearance position changes within those two business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted Dealing must be executed within two business days and clearance can be withdrawn before execution, which matters for pricing and settlement of any structured transaction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The names and addresses of Designated Persons will be supplied to Brambles' share registry from time to time, for the purpose of investigating compliance with this Policy and with the insider trading prohibition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any transfer of collared shares to a bank nominee or custodian is likely to be detected through registry monitoring.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Amended: ... and 3 July 2017
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lodged policy is dated July 2017 and may have been superseded; the bank should confirm the current version before relying on it.

BXB.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 2.4 bans Designated Persons (Directors, ELT, Band 4 and above, HQ staff and their connected persons) from trading any Brambles Derivatives, a term that expressly includes options granted by third parties and collars, so the purchased put and written call are prohibited outright over vested and unvested shares alike. Section 2.5 separately bans granting any pledge, lien, charge, mortgage or other encumbrance over Brambles Securities, so the loan secured on the collared shares is also prohibited, and the policy warns that a lender's enforcement sale in a Closed Period would itself be a breach. Neither ban has an approval or exemption route; the hardship and exceptional-circumstances discretion only covers sales or disposals during Prohibited Periods. The only financing left open is an investment loan that takes no security over Brambles Securities.

rules.section: 2 (Short Swing Profit and Hedging Transaction Prohibition)

No pre-approval is required for this tier, and no minimum shareholding floor is imposed.
rules.evidence: a Hedging Transaction of vested shares, options, restricted stock units, any other instrument provided as employee equity-based compensation or Company Securities, except as permitted in Section 3.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar that limits the economic risk of Company Securities falls within the Hedging Transaction definition and is therefore banned outright for Designated Persons. An outright sale of vested shares is not a Hedging Transaction and remains available in an Open Period with written pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation over vested holdings by a non-Designated Insider is treated as a Hedging Transaction: permitted only within an Open Period, without Inside Information, with notification to the Compliance Officer within 7 days after the Dealing.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere named and is not listed in the definition of Deal. A short position taken to limit the economic risk of a holding would in substance be caught by the Hedging Transaction ban for Designated Persons, but the policy itself does not say so.
Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the Deal definition, which reaches buying, selling, otherwise trading in, gifting, pledging, accepting and exercising Securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial instrument whose value is partly determined by the value of Company Securities and so a Security and a Dealing; where it provides a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities it is a Hedging Transaction and is banned outright for this tier.

rules.detail: For non-Designated Insiders a CFD over Company Securities is a Dealing in a Security. It may be entered in an Open Period without Inside Information and without a Compliance Officer prohibition; if it limits economic risk it is also a Hedging Transaction and attracts the 7-day notification, and the unvested hedging ban if it hedges unvested equity.
rules.evidence: An Insider and his or her Associates may Deal in Company Securities during an Open Period, but only if at that time: (a) the Insider or Associate is not in possession of Inside Information; and (b) the Compliance Officer has not prohibited such Insider or Associates from Dealing in the Company Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named and is not prohibited. Pledging Securities is expressly within the definition of Deal, so putting Company Securities up as margin collateral is a Dealing: it must occur in an Open Period, outside a Black-out Period, without Inside Information, and requires written approval by the Compliance Officer on not less than five ASX trading days' notice. The policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls and price triggers.

rules.detail: For non-Designated Insiders a margin loan pledge is a Dealing that may be done in an Open Period without Inside Information; no pre-clearance or notification is required unless the Insider is in doubt and applies under Section 10.

rules.detail: Granting a pledge over Company Securities is not separately prohibited but is expressly a Deal, so for Designated Persons it needs written Compliance Officer approval on five ASX trading days' notice, must be executed in the Open Period following approval and outside any Black-out Period, and subsequent confirmation must be given. Charges, liens and mortgages other than pledges are not named.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

rules.detail: A pledge by a non-Designated Insider is a Dealing permitted in an Open Period absent Inside Information or a Compliance Officer prohibition; pledging unvested plan securities is not separately addressed, though such securities are usually not transferable under the plan rules.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

The financing itself is not a Dealing, but the security granted over the shares is (pledging), so the transaction requires written pre-clearance for Designated Persons and must be executed within the Open Period following approval. No disclosure of financing arrangements is required beyond confirmation of the Dealing and, for Directors, Appendix 3Y notification of relevant-interest changes.

rules.detail: Secured financing is not addressed for non-Designated Insiders either; the pledge leg is a Dealing that may be done in an Open Period without Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedging ban for senior people
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person or one of his or her Associates must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are squarely a Hedging Transaction, so no director, CEO, CFO, Financial Controller or Vice President (or their family, family company or trust) can enter a collar at all, whether the shares are vested or not and whether the window is open or closed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging definition is economic, not instrument-based
bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging Transaction means Dealing in call or put options involving Company Securities or in other derivative Company Securities that provide a means to limit the economic risk of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It names call and put options directly and then sweeps in any other derivative that limits economic risk, so a bank cannot restructure the collar as a swap, prepaid forward or CFD to avoid it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exemption authority reaches the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee of the James Hardie Group may request a specific exemption from the prohibitions in Section 2 ... An exemption may be approved by the CFO or General Counsel, or in the case of an exemption for a Director or direct report to the CEO, by the Chairman of the Board or Audit Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only route to a collar for a Designated Person: the hedging ban sits in Section 2 and is therefore waivable, but only on hardship-style 'good reasons', only if it does not undermine the spirit of the Policy, and the waiver is reported to the Board.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging permitted for non-designated staff on notification only
bespoke_clauses.clause: An Insider or one of his or her Associates (other than a Designated Person) wishing to Deal in Company Securities through a Hedging Transaction of vested shares ... may only do so if such Dealing is within the Open Period and the Insider or his or her Associate notifies the Compliance Officer of such Dealing within 7 days after such Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Below Designated Person level a collar over vested shares is available with no pre-approval at all, provided it is struck inside the four-week Open Period and reported within 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal means buying, selling or otherwise trading in, and gifting, pledging, accepting or exercising Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited, but the security granted over the collared shares is itself a Dealing, so it must be struck in an Open Period and, for Designated Persons, pre-cleared in writing five ASX trading days in advance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no secured financing or margin lending ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, secured financing arrangements, forced sales by a lender, or price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy the funding leg is unrestricted in substance, so the obstacle to a funded collar here is entirely the hedge legs, not the loan.

bespoke_clauses.topic: short window and long lead time
bespoke_clauses.clause: Open Period means the period of four weeks following a quarterly profit announcement ... (such four-week period not beginning until two Australian Securities Exchange trading days after the announcement has been released to the market) ... not less than five Australian Securities Exchange trading days before the date of that intended Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a structure is permitted, the five-trading-day notice consumes a quarter of the four-week window, so pricing must be agreed well before the window opens and the trade re-priced on execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the Compliance Officer approves the intended Dealing, such Dealing must take place within the Open Period following the approval (or such other period specified by the Compliance Officer).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared pledge or unwind must settle before the Open Period closes, so a collar's roll, restrike or termination has to be scheduled against the quarterly calendar rather than a market date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short Swing Profit means any profit realised or expected to be realised by any Designated Person or any of his or her Associates from any purchase and sale, or any sale and purchase, of Company Securities within any period of less than six months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities include derivatives, even an exempted collar for a Designated Person could not be unwound, rolled or physically settled within six months of the opening legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means ... a family company of the Insider (i.e., a company in which an Insider, his or her domestic partner, a relative or family trust is a director, shareholder or adviser); or any trust or estate in which an Insider is a trustee, beneficiary or a director of a trustee or an adviser.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family company, family trust or an estate does not escape the Designated Person hedging ban, and the Insider must actively inform those persons of their obligations.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Compliance Officer may prohibit some or all Insiders and their Associates from Dealing in specific Securities ... The Compliance Officer may further prohibit one or more groups of Insiders and Associates from Dealing in Securities during certain periods, including Open Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An Open Period is not a guaranteed execution window: the Compliance Officer can close it for a group at any time, which must be treated as a condition precedent to pricing rather than a settled fact.

bespoke_clauses.clause: terminating or suspending an Insider's employment contract, and, if applicable, any such termination shall constitute a termination 'for cause' under such contract; or declaring the Insider ineligible for future participation in the James Hardie Group's equity incentive plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered by a Designated Person without an exemption is a for-cause termination event and forfeits future equity, so the bank should require written evidence of clearance or exemption before trading.

JHX.summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive of James Hardie without a specific exemption. Designated Persons, which expressly include all Directors, the CEO, CFO, Financial Controller and Vice Presidents, and their Associates 'must not engage in Dealings undertaken for Short Swing Profit or Hedging Transactions at any time', and the Hedging Transaction definition names call and put options and any other derivative that limits the economic risk of Company Securities, so both collar legs are banned outright regardless of vesting state or window. The only route is a Section 6 specific exemption from the Section 2 prohibitions, granted by the CFO or General Counsel (or, for a Director or a direct report to the CEO, the Chairman of the Board or the Audit Committee) on hardship-style good reasons that do not undermine the spirit of the Policy, and reported to the Board. The funding leg is by contrast unconstrained: the policy says nothing about margin lending, secured financing, margin calls or forced sales, and the only requirement is that the pledge, being within the definition of Deal, be pre-cleared in writing five ASX trading days ahead and executed inside the four-week Open Period that starts two trading days after a quarterly announcement. Below Designated Person level a collar over vested shares is genuinely available, needing only an Open Period execution, no Inside Information, and notification to the Compliance Officer within 7 days after dealing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restricted dealings bind only KMP and Lead Team
bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP and South32 Lead Team members must not undertake any of the following dealings ... (a) trade in derivative products ... (d) enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements ... (e) enter into any hedging arrangements that limit his or her exposure to the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivatives, hedging and secured financing bans are confined to KMP, South32 Lead Team members and their PCAs; a senior executive below the Lead Team faces only Insider Trading rules (and pre-approval plus closed periods if designated a Restricted Employee), so a funded collar is arguable for that population but not for the target directors and executives.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit his or her exposure to the Company's securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only ban hedging of unvested incentive securities, this prohibition covers a KMP's entire holding, so vesting the shares first does not open a route to a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing includes a wide range of transactions such as using the Company's shares as security for a loan and entering into any derivative contract which relates to the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the loan leg and the option legs of a funded collar are dealings, so each requires prior approval, falls inside the closed periods, and triggers same-day notification to Company Secretariat and disclosure to ASX, LSE, JSE and the FCA.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If, however, a member of the KMP South32 Lead Team or a Restricted Employee needs to deal (to sell but not buy) in securities during a closed period due to exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even in hardship there is no route to enter, roll or unwind a collar during a closed period, because buying (including buying a put or closing out a written call) is excluded; only an outright sale can be approved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the relevant approver may determine that this Policy does not apply to other types of dealings in respect of the Company's securities (for example: those listed in section 6.1 of ASX Listing Rules Guidance Note 27), provided that no such determination would breach any relevant law or regulation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a bank collar for a KMP, but it sits in the 'dealings excluded from this Policy' section rather than in section 6.9 and is illustrated only by routine GN27 exclusions, so it should not be relied on without a board-level waiver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approved dealing must occur within two business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and approval must be sought again.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved transaction must be priced and executed within two business days, which is tight for negotiating and documenting an OTC collar and loan, although the approver can specify a longer window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: company, a legal person, trust partnership or other entity, the managerial responsibilities of which are discharged by the KMP ... which is directly or indirectly controlled by such a person or is set up for the benefit of such a person, or the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to those of such a person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or the borrowing through an SPV, family trust or spouse does not escape the prohibitions, and KMP must file a list of these persons with the Company.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that is specified as a closed period for dealings from time to time. In particular, this could include a period specified as a closed period if required to do so by applicable law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Additional closed periods can be declared without notice and the Policy does not say they will be announced, so execution risk sits with the executive on any dated collar entry or unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vested shares released from the incentive plan fall squarely back under the Policy, including the section 6.9 hedging and secured financing bans, so there is no post-vesting freedom to collar them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Breaches of this Policy may also lead to disciplinary action being taken against the Employee, including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forfeiture of securities is an express sanction, which for a bank would put the collateral itself at risk if the structure were found to breach the Policy.

S32.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a South32 director, KMP or Lead Team member. Section 6.9 imposes a flat, approval-free ban on four things a funded collar requires: trading derivative products issued over or in respect of South32 securities, entering hedging arrangements that limit exposure to those securities, entering margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of them, and dealing on a short-term (three month) basis; the bans are not confined to unvested or plan securities and extend to spouses, controlled companies and trusts through the PCA definition. The only relief mechanisms are sale-only approvals in exceptional circumstances during a closed period and the open-ended section 8.2 power for the relevant approver to determine that the Policy does not apply to other types of dealings, which is illustrated only by routine Guidance Note 27 exclusions and should not be relied on without a board-level waiver. Below Lead Team level the position differs sharply: section 6.9 does not apply to ordinary Employees or notified Restricted Employees, for whom the option and loan legs are simply dealings requiring, at most, prior approval from the CEO or Company Secretary outside a closed period. Any transaction that were approved must be executed within two business days and, for KMP and their PCAs, notified to Company Secretariat by close of business on the day of dealing and on to ASX, LSE, JSE and the UK FCA.

tiers.name: Computershare Person
tiers.description: Any director, officer or employee of, or Contractor to, Computershare Limited or a member of the Computershare Group. This tier is bound only by Section C, the insider trading prohibition; the Prohibited Periods, Dealing Windows, clearance procedure, hedging ban, short-selling ban and secured lending notification in Section D apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: Each person listed in Schedule 1 (all Directors including the CEO, Company Secretaries, CFO, CIO, Group Treasurer, Group Investor Relations Manager, Group Financial Controller, Group Business Controller, Group Taxation Director, President Global Capital Markets, Group Head of Audit, Group Information Security and Risk Officer, Regional CEOs and Regional CFOs, Group Head of Communications, and other persons nominated by the Group CEO or Group CFO) plus any other person who is key management personnel of the Group within AASB 124. Subject to all Section D requirements.

tiers.name: Director
tiers.description: A director of Computershare, including the CEO. A Designated Person with two extra obligations: prior notice of any Dealing in a Dealing Window to the CEO (or the Company Secretary in the CEO's absence), and written advice of every Deal to the Company Secretary within two business days for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A lodgement.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: In relation to a Designated Person: their partner and the dependants of the Designated Person or their partner; a company or other entity of which the Designated Person is a director; a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Designated Person; and any other entity which the Designated Person has an ability to control. The Designated Person must make them aware of the Policy, of the Prohibited Periods, of the clearance procedures and of the duty to notify the Designated Person immediately after any Dealing.

clearance.evidence: A response to a request for clearance to Deal must be given to a Designated Person in writing (by email or otherwise) within two business days of the receipt of the request. A Designated Person who receives clearance to Deal from the Nominated Director in accordance with this procedure must Deal as soon as possible after receiving the Nominated Director's response

clearance.approver: CEO (or in his or her absence the Company Secretary) receives prior notice of Dealings in a Dealing Window; the Chairman of the Board is the Nominated Director for clearances, and the Chairman of the Risk and Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, who lodges the Appendix 3Y with ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A and discloses whether clearance was granted to Deal during a Prohibited Period
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as possible after the Dealing is transacted and in any event within two business days; ASX lodgement within five business days
clearance.evidence: A written advice (by email or otherwise) of any Deal in Computershare Securities by a Director must be provided to the Company Secretary as soon as possible after the Dealing is transacted and, in any event, within two business days after the Dealing is transacted.
It is the personal responsibility of each Computershare Person to ensure that they comply with the insider trading laws.

clearance.approver: Nominated Director, via the Designated Person
clearance.post_trade_to: the Designated Person
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after any Dealing in Computershare's Securities has been transacted
clearance.evidence: to notify them immediately after any Dealing in Computershare's Securities has been transacted.

short_term.basis: buying and selling within the same Dealing Window
carve_outs: Dealing relating to the vesting or exercise of options over, or rights to, Computershare Securities under an employee equity incentive plan and the subsequent sale of some or all of the underlying Securities within the same Dealing Window
short_term.evidence: a Designated Person must obtain clearance to Deal in accordance with the procedure set out in Section D.4 if they intend to buy and sell Computershare Securities within the same Dealing Window.
Each director, officer and employee of the Computershare Group is encouraged to be a long-term holder of Computershare Securities.

exceptions.approver: Nominated Director, in his or her sole discretion
exceptions.evidence: a Designated Person may apply for, and be granted, clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Computershare Securities during a Prohibited Period where they: are in severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances apply

exceptions.approver: Nominated Director
exceptions.evidence: where the Designated Person is compelled by court order, or otherwise by an overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to sell or otherwise dispose of the relevant Computershare Securities.

exceptions.approver: no approval required, but prior notice to the Nominated Director under D.11 is a condition
exceptions.evidence: an involuntary disposal of Computershare Securities that results from a lender exercising its rights under a secured lending arrangement provided that the Designated Person had, before the disposal, informed the Nominated Director of the risk of the disposal in accordance with Section D.11 of this Policy;

a Dealing by a Designated Person with an associated person whose interest in the Securities is to be treated by virtue of the Corporations Act as the Designated Person's interest such that there is no change in the beneficial interest in the Computershare Securities.

During a Prohibited Period, a Designated Person (or a trustee on behalf of the Designated Person) may acquire Computershare Securities under a non-discretionary trading plan ("Trading Plan") which has been established under, or in relation to, an employee equity incentive plan

exceptions.approver: Nominated Director for exercises and subsequent sales
exceptions.evidence: Where a Designated Person applies or subscribes for, is granted or acquires Securities (except Securities acquired on the exercise of Securities ...) under an employee equity incentive plan at a time that falls outside a Prohibited Period, the Designated Person is not required to seek clearance of those Dealings under Section D.

undertakings, elections or trading under an offer or an invitation which has been made to all or most shareholders, including a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back where the document that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer that has been publicly made for Computershare;
transfers of Computershare Securities held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary;

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price or loan-to-value trigger is specified. The trigger for notification is event-based: the lender has demanded payment and there is a risk that the demand cannot be satisfied without disposing of Computershare Securities.
financing_disclosure: Designated Person; on the lender demanding payment where there is a risk it cannot be met without disposing of Computershare Securities (not at inception, and not annually); the relevant Nominated Director; immediately

Director; any Deal (including entry into a Derivative); the Company Secretary, then ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A; within two business days of the Dealing, ASX lodgement within five business days, disclosing whether clearance was granted to Deal during a Prohibited Period
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: No minimum shareholding requirement. Section D.9 only encourages each director, officer and employee to be a long-term holder of Computershare Securities.

external_documents: Computershare Deferred Long Term Incentive Plan and other employee equity incentive plan rules (referred to but not set out; disposal restrictions on vested awards are determined under those rules)

ASX Listing Rule 3.19A notification
CPU.exemption_authority: The Nominated Director has sole discretion to grant clearance to sell (but not purchase) during a Prohibited Period on severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances, and must be satisfied the disposal is the only reasonable course of action. The Board may determine exceptional circumstances permitting cancellation of a Trading Plan during a Prohibited Period, and only the Board may amend the Policy. There is no general power to waive the D.5 hedging ban or the D.10 short selling ban.
jurisdiction_overlays: The Policy expressly does not deal with foreign law, while noting that foreign insider trading laws may apply to directors, officers and employees residing outside Australia

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The instrument the bank proposes is named in the Policy's own definitions, so there is no ambiguity that a collar is within scope and, over fully vested unrestricted Securities, within what D.5 permits.

bespoke_clauses.clause: once any applicable Computershare Securities have vested, such that any Computershare imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied (and any disposal restrictions on vested Securities have been lifted), Derivatives may be used in relation to those Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an express permission, not merely silence, so a collar over fully vested and unrestricted shares is contemplated by the Policy; the bank should obtain confirmation from the Company Secretary that all plan disposal restrictions on the specific parcel have lapsed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lending permitted with a distress-only notice
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must inform the relevant Nominated Director immediately if all of the following circumstances apply: the Designated Person holds Computershare Securities that have been provided as security in relation to a lending arrangement; circumstances have arisen in which the secured lender demands payment ...; and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Computershare Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no prohibition on the loan leg and no inception or annual disclosure, but the executive must give the Nominated Director immediate notice once the bank demands payment in circumstances where shares may have to be sold, and the facility documents should oblige the bank to alert the borrower in time for that notice.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale is an exempt dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of Computershare Securities that results from a lender exercising its rights under a secured lending arrangement provided that the Designated Person had, before the disposal, informed the Nominated Director of the risk of the disposal in accordance with Section D.11
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually favourable for a funded structure: lender enforcement, including during a Prohibited Period, is carved out of the Section D requirements entirely, but the carve-out is conditional on the D.11 notice having been given first, so a sudden enforcement without notice would put the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: clearance required even in an open window for derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to Section D.5 of this Policy, if a Designated Person intends to Deal in a Derivative over Computershare Securities during a Dealing Window then the Designated Person must obtain clearance to Deal in accordance with the procedure set out in Section D.4.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ordinary share trades in a Dealing Window need no clearance, but every derivative leg does, so entry, roll, restrike, partial unwind and physical settlement of the collar each require a separate written clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no fixed clearance validity, deal as soon as possible
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person who receives clearance to Deal from the Nominated Director in accordance with this procedure must Deal as soon as possible after receiving the Nominated Director's response
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no stated number of days for which a clearance remains valid, but the obligation to deal 'as soon as possible' means the collar should be pre-negotiated and priced so it can be executed immediately on clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If clearance to Deal is granted that clearance is not an approval of the proposed Dealing. Each Designated Person remains personally responsible for any decision to Deal and for their compliance with the insider trading laws and this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance gives the bank no comfort that the company has blessed the structure, so the bank cannot rely on it as a representation of policy compliance and should take its own compliance representations from the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing Window means: the four week period from ... the ASX trading day after the date on which Computershare's half-year financial results are released ... full-year financial results are released ... the annual general meeting is held
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an open-window policy: for most of the year a Designated Person is outside both a Dealing Window and a Prohibited Period and needs specific clearance under D.3, so scheduling collar entry and any unwind inside one of the three four-week windows is the low-friction path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: and any other period that may be designated as a prohibited period by the Board from time to time and notified to each Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An ad hoc Prohibited Period can block collar entry or a voluntary unwind at short notice, though it must be notified to the Designated Person, so the executive will know.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not enter into an arrangement to short sell Computershare Securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be fully covered by shares the executive actually holds; an overhedge, or a cash-settled structure over notional shares in excess of the holding, would breach D.10 even inside a Dealing Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Person means, in relation to a Designated Person: (a) the Designated Person's partner and dependants ...; (b) a company or other entity of which the Designated Person is a director; (c) a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Designated Person; and (d) any other entity which the Designated Person has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written by a family trust or controlled company is treated as within the Policy, so the same clearance and notification path applies wherever the collateral shares are held.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In accordance with ASX Listing Rule 3.19A, the Company Secretary will lodge with the ASX the necessary notification of the change in the Director's interest in Computershare Securities within five business days after the Dealing is transacted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar is a Deal in Securities, so it becomes publicly disclosed via Appendix 3Y within five business days, and the bank should expect the structure to be visible to the market.

CPU.summary: A funded collar is achievable for a Computershare Designated Person over fully vested Securities, and this is one of the most permissive policies in the set. Section D.5 bans hedging only of unvested incentive awards and vested awards still subject to disposal restrictions, and then expressly states that once hurdles are satisfied and disposal restrictions lifted, Derivatives may be used, with the definition of Derivatives naming collars outright. There is no prohibition on margin lending or secured financing: the loan leg is unregulated at inception, the only obligation being immediate notice to the Nominated Director once the lender demands payment in circumstances where Computershare Securities may have to be sold, and an involuntary disposal by the lender is then an exempt Dealing even in a Prohibited Period. Conditions are that every derivative leg needs prior written clearance from the Nominated Director (the Chairman of the Board for Directors, the CEO for other Designated Persons, responded to within two business days and dealt on as soon as possible), that entry falls outside the 15 June and 15 December Prohibited Periods and ideally inside one of the three four-week Dealing Windows, that the structure is fully covered by shares held so as not to offend the absolute short selling ban, and that a Director's dealing will be disclosed to the ASX within five business days.

REA.title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: directors, employees and contractors
tiers.description: Directors, employees and contractors of REA or any of its subsidiaries in any part of the world, including all permanent employees, contractors, consultants, secondees and casual employees. This tier is bound by the insider trading prohibition in section 3 only; the Blackout Periods, the speculative dealing prohibitions in section 5 and the clearance process in section 8 apply only to Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors including the CEO; members of the Executive Leadership Team; direct reports of the Executive Leadership Team including Executive Assistants; members of the Legal, Company Secretary, Strategy, Corporate Development and Communications teams and all employees with access to the monthly consolidated financial information; and any other employee nominated for a specified duration by the CEO, Company Secretary or CFO. Where section 5 refers to 'all other Restricted Persons' it means this group excluding Directors and Executive Leadership Team members, who face the stricter absolute bans.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of REA, including the CEO. A Restricted Person subject to the absolute hedging and secured financing bans in sections 5.2(a) and 5.3, to clearance by the Chair of the Board plus the CEO or Company Secretary (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the ARCC plus the CEO or Company Secretary), and to a duty to advise the Company Secretary within two business days of executing a cleared dealing.

tiers.name: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
tiers.description: Members of REA's Executive Leadership Team. Subject to the same absolute bans as Directors on hedging exposure to REA Securities and on margin loans and secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

tiers.name: Connected Parties
tiers.description: Any person a director, employee or contractor may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, in relation to a decision to deal in REA Securities, including spouse or partner and children, any family company or family trust the person or their close family members control or have an interest in, and any company, trust or partnership the person controls or in which they are a director, trustee or partner. Every substantive prohibition in sections 5.2 and 5.3 is expressed to bind Connected Parties directly, and clearance sought on their behalf is binding on them.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedges and derivatives are used to limit the economic risk associated with securities and include OTC products, contracts for difference, options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.

REA.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The REA Board, or the Chairman of the Board acting alone, may determine any other period to be a Blackout Period. The Policy does not say whether such a determination is announced or kept confidential, but it also provides that REA may monitor dealings and block dealings it considers to be in breach, and may apply blocks or restrictions on securities held under an employee share scheme by the scheme administrator.

rules.detail: Absolute ban with no clearance route and no vesting qualification: Directors and their Connected Parties must not hedge their exposure to REA Securities at all. The hedging definition expressly names collars and OTC products.
rules.evidence: Directors, members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not hedge their exposure to REA Securities;

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Identical absolute ban on hedging exposure to REA Securities, extending to Connected Parties.
rules.evidence: Directors, members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not hedge their exposure to REA Securities;

rules.detail: For Restricted Persons other than Directors and Executive Leadership Team members, hedging arrangements over vested REA Securities are prohibited only in the absence of prior written clearance, so clearance under section 8 makes them permissible. This is an express contemplation of a hedge over vested shares, not mere silence.
rules.evidence: all other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties are prohibited from hedging arrangements over: (i) vested REA Securities, unless they have received prior written clearance;

rules.detail: Hedging of REA Securities acquired under an employee share or equity incentive plan prior to vesting is banned outright, with no clearance route. For key management personnel the Policy notes this is also an offence under the Corporations Act.
rules.evidence: REA Securities acquired under an employee share or equity incentive plan operated by the Company, prior to vesting;

rules.detail: Vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under a plan cannot be hedged, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: REA Securities that are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee share or equity incentive plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: The hedging restrictions bind Connected Parties directly and in the same terms as the person they are connected to, so a family trust or controlled company of a Director cannot write the collar either.
rules.evidence: Directors, members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not hedge their exposure to REA Securities;

rules.detail: Section 5 is headed 'Other types of speculative dealing which this policy prohibits for Restricted Persons'; an employee or contractor who is not a Restricted Person is not subject to any hedging restriction under this Policy.

Section 5.2 is headed 'No hedging or other derivatives' and defines hedges and derivatives together to include OTC products, options, forward contracts, swaps, caps and collars. The ban on Directors hedging their exposure therefore captures both legs of an OTC collar directly, with no venue distinction and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Hedges and derivatives are used to limit the economic risk associated with securities and include OTC products, contracts for difference, options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Same absolute prohibition on OTC derivatives that limit economic risk in REA Securities.
rules.evidence: Hedges and derivatives are used to limit the economic risk associated with securities and include OTC products, contracts for difference, options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.

rules.detail: An OTC put and call over vested, unrestricted REA Securities is a derivative that limits economic risk and so falls under 5.2(b)(i), which permits it with prior written clearance. Independently, entering the derivative is a dealing in REA Securities (financial products created over REA securities) and every dealing by a Restricted Person requires clearance at all times, even outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person, you must seek prior written clearance (see section 8 below) before you deal in any REA Securities. This clearance process applies at all times, even outside Blackout Periods.

rules.detail: No derivative may be written over unvested plan securities or over vested securities under a holding lock, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: REA Securities acquired under an employee share or equity incentive plan operated by the Company, prior to vesting;

rules.detail: For a person who is not a Restricted Person, creating a hedge over REA Securities is a dealing but is restricted only by the insider trading prohibition; no Blackout Period or clearance requirement applies.
rules.evidence: Deal or dealing has a wide meaning and includes: buying, selling or applying for securities; creating a hedge, security interest or other financial interest over securities

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar plus loan or similar structure limits economic risk in REA Securities and so is a hedge banned by 5.2(a), and any secured borrowing element is separately banned by 5.3.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

rules.detail: For Restricted Persons below Director and Executive Leadership Team level, both the hedge over vested securities and the grant of security or secured lending arrangement are permitted with prior written clearance, so a full monetisation is contemplated subject to clearance for each element.
rules.evidence: All other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not, unless they have prior written clearance: (a) grant any security or any other rights over REA Securities

rules.detail: Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not short sell REA Securities. Unlike the short-term dealing limb, the short-selling limb carries no clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not: ... (b) short-sell any REA Securities.

rules.detail: The short selling ban applies only to Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties.

Securities lending or stock borrowing is not named anywhere and does not appear in the definition of dealing, although lending REA Securities to a bank would arguably involve creating a financial interest over securities.

Contracts for difference are named in the definition of hedges and derivatives, so they fall within the absolute ban on Directors and Executive Leadership Team members hedging their exposure to REA Securities.
rules.evidence: Hedges and derivatives ... include OTC products, contracts for difference, options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.

rules.detail: A CFD over vested REA Securities requires prior written clearance under 5.2(b)(i); a short CFD would still offend the short selling ban and a CFD closed within three months the short-term dealing rule.
rules.evidence: all other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties are prohibited from hedging arrangements over: (i) vested REA Securities, unless they have received prior written clearance;

rules.detail: Directors and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security. The only carve-out is for arrangements duly approved under earlier versions of the Policy, which are grandfathered.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities. This prohibition does not apply to arrangements which were duly approved under earlier versions of this policy.

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Identical ban, subject to the same grandfathering of arrangements approved under earlier versions of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

rules.detail: For all other Restricted Persons, entering a new margin loan, transferring REA Securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling REA Securities to satisfy a margin call each require prior written clearance rather than being prohibited.
rules.evidence: All other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not, unless they have prior written clearance: ... rules.detail: Creating a security interest over securities is itself a dealing under the definition, and for Directors and Executive Leadership Team members any secured financing arrangement in respect of REA Securities is prohibited outright. Section 5.3(a), which allows the grant of security with clearance, is expressed to apply only to 'all other Restricted Persons'.
rules.evidence: Deal or dealing has a wide meaning and includes: buying, selling or applying for securities; creating a hedge, security interest or other financial interest over securities

rules.evidence: All other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not, unless they have prior written clearance: (a) grant any security or any other rights over REA Securities, including over any 'unvested' REA Securities;

rules.detail: Creating a security interest is a dealing, but section 5 binds only Restricted Persons, so an employee outside that group faces only the insider trading prohibition when pledging REA Securities.
rules.evidence: Deal or dealing has a wide meaning and includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest or other financial interest over securities

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans: it extends to any secured financing arrangement in respect of REA Securities, which is exactly the loan leg of a funded collar. There is no clearance route and no hardship waiver, only grandfathering of arrangements duly approved under earlier versions of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

rules.evidence: enter into any margin loan, margin lending or other secured lending arrangement in respect of REA Securities – this includes not: (i) entering into any new arrangement; (ii) transferring any REA Securities into an existing margin loan account; or (iii) selling REA Securities to satisfy any margin loan call.

rules.detail: The prohibition on Directors and Executive Leadership Team members is expressed to bind their Connected Parties, which include any family trust or controlled company, so the borrower cannot be an SPV or family vehicle.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's target population, directors and executive leadership, is subject to an absolute hedging ban with no clearance route, while a collar over vested shares is expressly available with clearance to Restricted Persons one level below them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Parties must not enter into a margin loan using REA Securities as security, or enter into secured financing arrangements in respect of REA Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is prohibited outright for directors and executive leadership, independently of the hedging ban, so neither restructuring the derivative nor unsecuring the facility rescues the trade for that tier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or dealing has a wide meaning and includes: buying, selling or applying for securities; creating a hedge, security interest or other financial interest over securities; transferring legal ownership of securities (even where beneficial ownership does not change)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both granting the security and creating the hedge are dealings in their own right, so for a Restricted Person each requires separate prior written clearance and each falls inside the four Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All other Restricted Persons and their Connected Parties must not, unless they have prior written clearance: (a) grant any security or any other rights over REA Securities, including over any 'unvested' REA Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, unvested shares may be pledged by a non-Director Restricted Person with clearance, even though hedging those same unvested shares is banned outright, so a lender could take security without the borrower being able to hedge the exposure.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank is exempt from the Blackout Periods and the clearance requirement altogether, and unlike some policies there is no precondition of prior notice, so lender remedies are unusually clean where the underlying facility is itself permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Blackout Periods are: (a) from the close of trading on 31 March until 10:00am on the trading day after REA announces its "Q3" quarterly results ... REA.summary: A funded collar is not available to an REA director or Executive Leadership Team member. Section 5.2(a) bans them and their Connected Parties from hedging their exposure to REA Securities at all, with the hedging definition naming OTC products and collars specifically, and section 5.3 separately bans them from margin loans and any secured financing arrangement in respect of REA Securities; neither prohibition has a clearance route or hardship waiver, and the only relief is grandfathering of arrangements duly approved under earlier versions of the Policy. For Restricted Persons below that level the answer is different and unusually permissive: a hedge over vested REA Securities and the grant of security or a secured lending arrangement, including over unvested shares, are each permitted with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, valid for five business days and revocable at any time before dealing. Any such structure must sit outside REA's four quarterly Blackout Periods, must not involve short selling or a buy and sell within three months without further clearance, and must not touch securities that are unvested or under a plan holding lock, which cannot be hedged at all. Lender enforcement is a helpful carve-out, being exempt from both blackouts and clearance, but a borrower selling to meet a margin call needs clearance, and a director's cleared dealing must be reported to the Company Secretary within two business days for ASX disclosure.

FPH.summary: A funded collar over vested shares is possible under this 2013 policy. The purchased put and written call are financial products created over FPHC securities and therefore 'Restricted Securities', so a Restricted Person (director, CEO direct report, KMP or their controlled trust or company) must notify the CFO in writing and obtain consent from two directors or a director and the CFO, execute within 15 trading days, deal outside the black-out periods (30 September to the half-year results release, 30 days before balance date to the full-year results release, and 30 days before a prospectus), hold no material information, and advise the CFO promptly afterwards. The loan secured on the collared shares faces no restriction: margin lending, secured financing, hedging and encumbrances are not regulated, and a secured lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the additional dealing restrictions (though still subject to insider trading law). Non-Restricted employees need no consent at all. Unwind, roll or physical settlement of the collar by the executive is a fresh dealing requiring new consent outside black-outs, and the 2013 date suggests confirming the policy remains current.

ORG.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The unfunded derivative legs (purchased put and written call) over vested shares are a Dealing that Directors may enter with prior written clearance from the Chairman and Company Secretary (Manager and Company Secretary for ELT and their direct reports), executed within 2 business days, outside the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods and any confidential Additional Prohibition, and not over plan securities that remain unvested or subject to performance hurdles. However, section 7.1 expressly bans margin lending and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Origin Securities for all personnel and their Associates, with no exemption authority, so a loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright. A lender's forced sale in a Closed Period is a serious breach that may lead to dismissal, and there is no hardship relief. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban, and any unwind or settlement is itself a Dealing requiring fresh clearance.

SUN.title: Suncorp Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Suncorp Directors, Employees and Contractors
tiers.description: All statutory directors of Suncorp Group Limited and its controlled entities, all full-time, part-time and casual employees, and all consultants, contractors and secondees. This is the widest tier: the insider trading prohibition and the hedging ban in section 5.1 apply to it without differentiation, but closed periods, clearance and the short-term dealing and short selling bans do not.

tiers.name: Prescribed Persons
tiers.description: Persons who because of their seniority or position are likely to become involved with key financial, operational and strategic information about Suncorp, including all Suncorp Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team (together Suncorp's KMP), the Company Secretary, Executive General Managers and selected Executive Managers, all Executive Assistants and Executive Officers of those groups, and any other person nominated by an ELT member, the Company Secretary, an Executive General Manager or an Executive Manager. Subject to Closed Periods, clearance, the short-term dealing and short selling bans and margin loan review.

tiers.name: Suncorp Directors
tiers.description: Statutory directors of Suncorp. A subset of Prescribed Persons, distinguished for clearance (Suncorp Chairman or delegate; the Chairman's own requests go to the Audit Committee Chairman), for the requirement that even no-change-of-beneficial-owner transfers still need clearance, and for post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within three business days.

tiers.name: Executive Leadership Team
tiers.description: The senior executive positions reporting directly to the Group CEO. A subset of Prescribed Persons, distinguished only by the obligation to notify the Company Secretary of any Dealing within three business days so the Company Secretary can report to the Board.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A Prescribed Person's spouse or partner, their or their partner's dependent children, anyone else in the family whom the Prescribed Person may be expected to influence or be influenced by in Dealings with Securities, and a company, trust or entity that the Prescribed Person or any such family member controls or has an interest in. Connected Persons are subject to the same Closed Period, clearance, short-term dealing, short selling and margin loan restrictions as the Prescribed Person, who must make their clearance requests, waiver applications and notifications for them.

rules.section: 5.1; Key Terms (Security or Securities, Deal or Dealing)
rules.detail: An OTC put or call over Suncorp shares is a Security in its own right, so writing or buying it is a Dealing that would otherwise need clearance outside Closed Periods. But because the pair is designed to limit economic risk of a holding, section 5.1's hedging ban applies and the collar legs are prohibited outright rather than merely clearable.
rules.evidence: derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities, whether or not the securities or the derivative products are issued or created by Suncorp or by third parties.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Suncorp Securities are expressly within the definition of Securities, so acquiring or disposing of them is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance, outside Closed Periods and the Restricted List. Permitted only where the derivative is not itself designed to limit economic risk of a Suncorp holding (5.1) and does not amount to short-term Dealing or short selling (5.2).
rules.evidence: Outside of Closed Periods, Prescribed Persons and their Connected Persons are required to obtain clearance before Dealing in Suncorp Securities (unless the proposed Dealing falls into an Exempt Dealing category set out in Section 3).

rules.detail: Absolute, tier-wide hedging ban with no clearance or waiver route. It is not confined to plan or unvested securities: it reaches any 'holdings in Suncorp Securities' and expressly extends to unvested performance rights, so vested unrestricted shares are covered too. There is no venue limit and no exception for a collar.
rules.evidence: Directors, Employees and Contractors are prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.

rules.detail: Unvested performance rights are expressly named as within the hedging ban, putting beyond doubt that awards not yet vested cannot be hedged.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into a hedging transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of holdings in Suncorp Securities, including unvested performance rights.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar structure is designed to limit the economic risk of a Suncorp holding and so is caught by the section 5.1 hedging ban; forward contracts are also given as the example of prohibited short-term Dealing in 5.2(a).
rules.evidence: entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban for Prescribed Persons and Connected Persons, defined as borrowing the security and selling it to profit from an anticipated fall. No carve-outs and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Short Selling of Suncorp Securities. This is the practice of attempting to profit from an anticipated drop in the price of Securities by borrowing the Security and selling it in anticipation of later being able to buy the Securities at a lower price to close out their short position at a profit.

rules.detail: Lending out Suncorp Securities is nowhere prohibited or named as a Dealing. Borrowing securities appears only descriptively inside the definition of short selling. The Dealing definition's limb on granting a security interest and its limb on disposing of a beneficial interest may reach a title-transfer stock loan, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for differences relating to Suncorp shares are expressly named as Securities. A CFD taken to offset a holding is a hedging transaction banned by 5.1, and a CFD is in practice a short-term Dealing under 5.2(a); a short CFD would also engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: derivative products (including but not limited to warrants, exchange-traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) relating to those securities

rules.detail: Margin loans are not banned. A new or increased Margin Loan over Suncorp Securities is a Dealing (granting a security interest) requiring clearance, and the request is escalated to the Suncorp Chairman or the Group CEO personally, who may impose whatever terms and conditions they see fit because of forced-sale risk. The heading says Prescribed Persons 'may be restricted', so clearance is discretionary and may be refused without reasons.
rules.evidence: The Suncorp Chairman, or the Group CEO, will review any request for waiver or clearance to Deal by Prescribed Persons or their Connected Persons which involves entering into a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction.

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, lien, charge or other security interest over Suncorp Securities is expressly listed as an example of Dealing, so it needs prior written clearance and cannot be done in a Closed Period. Where the security interest supports a financial transaction, section 6 escalates it to the Chairman or Group CEO.
rules.evidence: granting a mortgage, lien, charge or other security interest (such as a Margin Loan) over Securities;

rules.detail: Section 6 is not limited to margin loans: it reaches 'other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction', which squarely captures a loan secured on collared shares. There is no prohibition, only mandatory review by the Chairman or Group CEO with power to impose conditions, and the underlying clearance can be refused in Suncorp's discretion without reasons.
rules.evidence: which involves entering into a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction.

rules.detail: Buying and selling the same Security within six months is banned, as is entering into any other short term Dealing, with forward contracts given as the example. Carve-outs for the sale of ordinary shares acquired on exercise of a right or option under a Suncorp employee share plan, and for off-market transactions with no effective change in beneficial owner.
rules.evidence: Short-Term Dealing of Suncorp Securities: means buying and selling the same Security within a six month period and entering into any other short term Dealings (for example, forward contracts) in relation to Securities.

clearance.approver: Suncorp Group Chief Executive Officer or delegate; applications lodged with the Company Secretary

exceptions.approver: Suncorp Chairman, Audit Committee Chairman or Group CEO (or delegate) depending on applicant

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No LVR or price trigger is specified. The policy identifies forced-sale risk as the reason for escalation and gives the Chairman or Group CEO an open-ended power to impose terms and conditions on the financing: 'A margin call or a default on a Margin Loan could result in the need for a forced sale of Securities, at a time outside of a Prescribed Person's control. Therefore the Suncorp Chairman or the Group CEO may impose terms and conditions on such Dealings as they see fit.'
financing_disclosure: Prescribed Persons and Connected Persons: at inception of a new or increased Margin Loan or other use of Suncorp Securities as collateral in a financial transaction, the request is made to the Company Secretary and reviewed by the Suncorp Chairman or the Group CEO before the arrangement may be entered into (section 6).

Suncorp Directors and Executive Leadership Team: after any Dealing (which includes granting a security interest over Suncorp Securities) by them or their Connected Persons, to the Company Secretary, within three business days (section 4).

Prescribed Persons: must keep, and produce to the Company Secretary on request, a register of every Dealing by themselves and their Connected Persons with supporting material such as contract notes (section 4, Record keeping).
