SGH.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or its delegate may determine 'any other period' to be a blackout period for the purposes of the policy. The policy does not state whether such a determination is confidential or how it is communicated.

rules.detail: Options and other financial products issued over SGH shares by third parties, associated products, and products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are all defined as SGH securities. There is no venue restriction and no outright ban, so an OTC put bought from a bank and a call written to it are dealings that a designated employee may do inside a window period, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the relevant approver.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products; Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over SGH shares are treated identically; the definition of SGH securities draws no distinction between listed and OTC products.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products

rules.detail: During blackout periods the ban on dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities is absolute for Executives and designated staff, and unlike the ordinary blackout ban it carries no exceptional circumstances relief. Outside blackout periods the ordinary window and clearance regime applies.
rules.evidence: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.

rules.detail: Employees who are neither Executives nor designated employees are not subject to the window periods or the prior clearance requirement. They are bound only by the insider trading restriction and by the general blackout-period ban, from which they may seek an exceptional-circumstances waiver from the SGH Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: In addition, designated employees are permitted to deal in SGH securities only as follows

rules.detail: Remarkably, the policy contains no prohibition on hedging. Products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply brought within the definition of SGH securities, so hedging is regulated like any other dealing: inside a window period, or outside it with prior written clearance from the relevant approver, and never during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: There is no ban on hedging unvested or unexercised employee share plan entitlements, which is unusual for an ASX policy. Participation in an SGH Employee Share Plan itself needs no approval or notification, but dealing in shares attained from employee share plans remains subject to the policy, so a hedge referencing plan securities is a dealing in SGH securities requiring a window or clearance.
rules.evidence: Dealing in shares attained from employee share plans is still subject to this policy.

rules.detail: Restricted shares are recognised (lifting restrictions on restricted shares needs no approval) but no separate hedging or encumbrance restriction attaches to them; the ordinary window and clearance regime governs.
rules.evidence: A SGH Group employee is not required to seek approval or provide notification in connection with participation in any SGH Employee Share Plan, which includes: ... Lifting restrictions on restricted shares.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a collar-plus-loan, prepaid forward or similar is both a financial product limiting the economic risk of holding SGH shares and, where secured, a dealing pursuant to a lending arrangement. Both limbs point to the same answer: written clearance from the relevant approver, which may be granted subject to conditions.
rules.evidence: Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy. A short sale would still be a 'sell' and therefore a dealing subject to the window, clearance and blackout regime, but there is no separate prohibition on it.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned and are outside the definition of Deal, which covers only buying and selling and procuring others to buy or sell.

CFDs are not named but a contract for difference over SGH shares is a financial product issued over SGH shares by a third party, or an associated product, and so is an SGH security. Dealing in it therefore requires a window period or prior written clearance, and is absolutely barred for Executives and designated staff in a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted, not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling SGH securities held in a margin loan account are each dealings requiring written clearance from the relevant approver, who may impose conditions. The employee must not participate in the decision on their own application.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in SGH securities by a SGH Group employee pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must comply with this policy. Such dealings may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account and selling SGH securities held in a margin loan account.

rules.detail: Granting security over SGH securities is not itself within the definition of Deal, but section 5 treats entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities and transferring securities into a margin loan account as dealings requiring written clearance. An encumbrance unconnected with a lending arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Such dealings may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: Only margin lending arrangements are named. A bank loan secured on SGH shares is not expressly covered, but section 5 is drafted broadly around 'any dealing in SGH securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement' and the prudent reading, consistent with the section 8 carve-out for secured lender enforcement, is that a share-secured facility must be cleared in the same way. There is no prohibition on secured financing anywhere in the policy.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in SGH securities by a SGH Group employee pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must comply with this policy.

rules.detail: The policy contains no short-term trading, speculative trading or minimum holding period restriction of any kind. The only timing constraints are the window periods, the blackout periods and the two-business-day validity of a clearance.

SGH.exemption_authority: The approver named in the section 3 table (and the SGH Company Secretary for non-designated employees) may grant a written waiver to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances, being where the approver is satisfied the proposed dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. The Board or its delegate may determine any other circumstance to be exceptional and may determine additional blackout periods. The one exemption expressly withheld is the blackout-period ban on Executives and designated staff dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging. Instead, 'Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares' are simply included in the definition of SGH securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the key enabling feature: a collar is regulated as an ordinary dealing needing a window or clearance, rather than banned, and there is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities either.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute blackout ban on derivative products
bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll, unwind or any adjustment involving the option legs is absolutely impossible in a blackout period, with no hardship or court-order relief, so the bank must build hard date constraints into the trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any designated employee must obtain clearance in writing from the relevant approver detailed in the table in Section 3 for any proposed dealing in SGH securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... Clearance may be granted subject to any conditions the approver determines appropriate.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted with clearance rather than prohibited, and the approver's power to impose conditions gives the company a way to protect itself rather than refuse outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy does not apply to: ... A disposal of SGH securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a margin lending arrangement, where this policy has been complied with in relation to the margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is outside the policy, but only if the underlying facility was itself properly cleared, so the bank should make clearance a condition precedent and retain evidence of it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance may be given in any written form and is effective for two business days after it has been given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the loan must be documented in advance and executed within two business days of clearance, so pricing and legal work must be complete before the approval is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the period between 24 hours and 30 working days after the release of SGH's Half Yearly Results announcement ... Annual Results announcements ... and the close of the SGHs Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Three 30-working-day windows a year give ample scope to strike or unwind a collar without needing discretionary clearance at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A designated employee must not be involved in a decision regarding their own application for clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a Chairman or CEO collar the approval must come from the Lead Independent Director or ARC Chair, so the bank should verify who signed the clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no short-term or speculative trading rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy imposes no minimum holding period and no restriction on short-term or speculative dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor is unconstrained by the policy, so short-dated or rolling structures are not objectionable on their face.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal includes buying and selling, as well as procuring others to buy or sell.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting security is not literally a Deal, so section 5 rather than the general definition is what brings the loan and any share transfer into the clearance net; a pledge unconnected to a lending arrangement sits in a gap.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of designated employees must comply with the policy as if they were a designated employee ... A breach of this policy, including a breach by an associate, will be regarded as serious misconduct.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or superannuation fund attracts the identical window, clearance and blackout constraints and the employee bears the consequences.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All designated employees and their associates must obtain approval prior to trading in the securities of listed entities in which SGH has a Substantial Interest (including controlled and associated entities) [Appendix 1: Beach Energy (BPT), Boral (BLD), Seven West Media (SWM)].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over Beach Energy, Boral or Seven West Media shares held by an SGH designated employee also requires prior approval under this policy.

SGH.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, and this is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the purpose. There is no hedging prohibition at all: products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply defined as SGH securities, so the put and call legs are dealings that a designated employee may execute inside one of the three 30-working-day window periods following the half year results, annual results and AGM, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the approver named in the section 3 table. Margin lending is likewise expressly permitted with written clearance, which may be granted subject to conditions, and a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is carved out of the policy entirely provided the facility itself was cleared, which protects the bank on enforcement. The two hard constraints are that no Executive or designated staff member may deal in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities during a blackout period, with no exceptional circumstances relief, and that clearance lapses after two business days, so the trade must be fully documented before approval is sought. There is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities and no short-term trading or minimum holding rule, so vesting state and tenor are not obstacles.

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Company. Same substantive prohibitions as directors; clearance is sought from the Secretary. No sub-tier of executives, KMP or 'restricted persons' is created.

LYC.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No separate ad hoc blackout power is conferred. The Chairman and Secretary retain a residual discretion to withhold clearance within an open period where undisclosed price sensitive information exists: they 'will generally allow' dealing 'unless there is in existence price sensitive information that has not been disclosed because of an ASX Listing Rule exception' (7.1), and no dealing may proceed until the Chairman or Secretary 'has indicated in writing that there is no impediment' (6.1(4)). The policy does not say whether a refusal or the reason for it is confidential.

rules.detail: Section 14 is an express derivatives rule but it bites only in prohibited periods: trading in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities is prohibited during prohibited periods, which under 7.3 means all time outside the three-week open windows. Outside those prohibited periods a derivative is permitted, subject to the general 6.1 gateway (no price sensitive information, advise the Chairman or Secretary, written confirmation of no impediment). No venue limitation is drawn, so an OTC put and call written by a bank is covered on the same footing as an exchange-traded option.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: During a prohibited period (all time other than the three-week windows in 7.1 and a 9.2 exceptional-circumstances clearance) an OTC collar cannot be entered, amended, rolled or settled. Section 9.2 relief is confined to a sale of securities and does not extend to derivative trading.
rules.evidence: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute, at all times ban, but narrowly drawn: it catches only the hedging of options issued under an employee option plan before those options vest. It does not by its terms extend to unvested performance rights or unvested shares, nor to options after vesting.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.

rules.detail: Hedging vested holdings is not named. The 13.2 ban stops at vesting, so by negative implication hedging vested options and shares is not prohibited; it is instead controlled as trading in a financial product over the Company's securities (14.1, barred in prohibited periods) and by the 6.1 clearance gateway. The policy does not define hedging or 'limiting economic risk' and draws no vested-but-locked category.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or collar is an agreement in relation to shares in the Company and so a Deal In Securities, and is also a financial product created over the Company's securities under 14.1. It therefore needs the 6.1 written no-impediment confirmation and must be entered inside a 7.1 open window.
rules.evidence: Deal In Securities means apply for, buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into agreements in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company and includes procuring another person to do any of these things

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere named and is not listed in the definition of Deal In Securities. A short sale would still be a 'sell' of securities in the Company and so a Dealing subject to 6.1 and the closed-period regime, and closing a short position would in practice engage the at all times short-term trading ban in 13.1, but neither is stated.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere and are not swept into the definition of Deal In Securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Lynas shares is a financial product created over or in respect of the Company's securities and so is barred during prohibited periods by 14.1 and needs 6.1 clearance in an open window; in practice a CFD would also be characterised as short-term trading, which 13.1 bans at all times.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named and is not prohibited. The policy positively contemplates that directors and employees may have securities pledged to a secured lender, because it carves a lender's enforcement sale out of the policy altogether. There is no disclosure obligation, price trigger guidance, cap on the proportion of the holding that may be pledged, or requirement to notify the company of a facility.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Lynas securities is not named and is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, which reaches applications, purchases, sales and agreements in relation to securities. Charging shares to a bank as collateral is therefore not itself a Dealing needing clearance, and the exclusion of secured lender enforcement sales confirms that encumbrances are contemplated.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on secured financing of any kind, whether a margin loan or a bespoke facility secured on Lynas shares, and no approval, notification or scope limit. The only provision on the subject is the excluded trading item protecting the borrower from breach when the lender enforces.
rules.evidence: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: Blanket, at all times ban on short-term trading in the Company's securities, with no defined holding period, no LIFO or intention test and no carve-out for plan securities. The absence of a definition leaves the boundary to the Chairman and Secretary at the 6.1 clearance stage.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

LYC.exemption_authority: The board may grant a specific exemption from the policy: directors and employees 'should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board' (2.2). Separately, the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director may clear a sale, but not a purchase, in exceptional circumstances where it is the only reasonable course of action available (9.2), and only if the person is not in possession of undisclosed price sensitive information (9.5).

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the single most collar-friendly clause in the policy: the bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares, including a sale in a closed period, falls outside the policy altogether, so the executive does not breach by reason of the lender enforcing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no margin lending, secured financing, pledge or encumbrance prohibition of any kind, and no disclosure obligation in respect of any such facility.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unrestricted, which is unusual among ASX policies and removes the usual blocking provision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are financial products over Lynas securities, so entry, amendment, roll, unwind and any cash or physical settlement of the collar must all be timed to fall inside a three-week open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lynas is closed by default and open only for three weeks after results, the AGM or a prospectus, so there may be as little as four short windows a year in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given by the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director for the director or employee to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he or she otherwise would not be permitted to do so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is confined to selling, so it cannot be used to buy back a written call, close out a put or enter a collar outside a window; only an outright sale of the underlying can be cleared.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested options
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is confined to unvested employee options, so a collar over vested shares is not caught by it, but unvested option entitlements must be excluded from the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no defined holding period, a short-dated collar or one with early termination or roll features risks being characterised as short-term trading, so a long tenor and confirmation from the Chairman or Secretary at clearance are advisable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so; and the proposed Dealing is permitted under paragraph 7.1 or 9.2.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy sets no window within which a cleared trade must be executed and no express revocation right, so the bank should document that the written no-impediment confirmation is current at pricing and at each subsequent leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: directors and employees should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The board can exempt a specific transaction from the policy entirely, which offers a route to sanction a collar whose timing or structure does not fit the narrow windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy has been implemented to prevent the incidence of 'insider trading' ... by directors and employees and persons associated with any of them. ... a director or employee must not recommend or otherwise suggest to any person (including a spouse, relative, friend, trustee of a family trust or directors of a family company) that they buy or sell securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Associates are referred to in the introduction but no associate is defined and no operative rule binds them, so a collar entered by a spouse or family trust sits in an untested area rather than a clearly permitted or prohibited one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors must notify the company secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering the collar may change the director's relevant interest, or be treated as doing so on physical settlement, triggering immediate notice to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y within 5 Business Days that will disclose the structure publicly.

LYC.summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable under this policy, which is markedly more permissive than most ASX policies on the financing leg. There is no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, pledging or encumbering Lynas securities, granting security is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, and paragraph 8.1(6) expressly excludes from the policy a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so the bank's enforcement sale would not put the executive in breach even in a closed period. The derivative legs are the constraint: a put and call over Lynas shares are financial products created over the Company's securities and cannot be traded during prohibited periods (14.1), and since 7.3 makes every period a closed period except the three weeks following results, the AGM or a prospectus, entry, roll, unwind and settlement must each be timed into one of those narrow windows and preceded by written confirmation of no impediment from the Chairman (directors) or Secretary (employees). The 13.2 hedging ban reaches only employee options before vesting, so vested shares may be collared, but the undefined at all times ban on short-term trading in 13.1 argues for a long tenor and for clearing the structure explicitly. Out-of-window relief under 9.2 covers only a sale of securities, not derivative dealings, so no exceptional-circumstances route exists for an emergency unwind, and directors should expect the position to surface through immediate notification to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y.

No venue limit, so an OTC put or call written by a bank is squarely caught. There is no clearance route: section 4.2.3 clearance is a gateway to dealing outside a Closed Period, not a waiver of the 4.2.5 prohibition, and the 4.2.7 exceptional circumstances power relieves only against dealing during a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons are not permitted at any time (including outside any Closed Period) to enter into any hedging instruments or arrangements regarding or derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause defeats the funded collar: both the purchased put and the written call are derivative financial products issued over APA Securities held by the executive, and the ban is absolute in time, indifferent to vesting, and has no clearance or exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons may include APA Securities in a diversified portfolio under a margin loan facility or secured financing arrangement provided that: the facility or arrangement does not permit title to the APA Securities to be transferred.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even setting the derivatives ban aside, the loan leg fails on its own terms: a facility secured solely on the collared APA parcel is not a diversified portfolio, and any title-transfer collateral or rehypothecation right is expressly prohibited, so only a non-title-transfer security interest inside a broader portfolio facility is permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any APA Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person, or any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unvested and holding-locked securities are unavailable as collateral in any structure, and the words 'directly or indirectly' and 'or any third party' block back-to-back or guarantee arrangements over that stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: to avoid doubt, the terms of this policy will continue to apply to the relevant APA Securities, including the requirement that they not be disposed of in a Closed Period unless permission for such disposal is granted pursuant to section 4.2.7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A margin call or enforcement sale during a Closed Period is not an excluded dealing and requires exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman, so a lender cannot rely on unfettered enforcement rights and the borrower bears the timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to undertake a proposed dealing will be valid for three business days or until a Closed Period commences, whichever is the shorter period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing in the underlying must be priced and executed within three business days, and a clearance may be withdrawn if circumstances change, which constrains any multi-leg execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The decision to give or refuse clearance is in the absolute discretion of the Recipient and is final and binding on the Applicant, and reasons for the decision need not be provided. ... If clearance is refused, the Applicant must keep the fact of that refusal confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no obligation to explain, and the executive cannot tell a bank counterparty why a transaction cannot proceed, so financing documents should not require disclosure of the reason for a refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the guiding principle is that Directors and Designated Persons who purchase APA Securities should intend, at the time of acquisition, to continue to hold the purchased APA Securities for at least the next 12 months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any structure with an economic tenor of under 12 months, or that contemplates repurchasing securities delivered under the collar, risks being treated as short-term or speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.topic: same open period buy and sell
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons must not both buy and sell APA Securities in the same “open” period between two consecutive Closed Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of a collar combined with any purchase in the same open window would breach this rule, so delivery and any repurchase must straddle a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: APA Group requires that Directors and Designated Persons take all reasonable steps to cause their respective Related Parties to comply with this section 4.2 as if they were Directors or Designated Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared stock through a spouse, resident child, family trust, superannuation fund or significantly influenced company does not escape the hedging ban or the financing conditions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivative financial products issued over any APA Securities held by the Director or Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by reference to securities held, so a cash-settled index or basket derivative not referable to a held parcel is arguably outside 4.2.5, though it would still face the short selling and short-term trading prohibitions in 4.2.4.

bespoke_clauses.clause: other persons specified from time to time by the Managing Director ... The Company Secretary will operate a process for regularly reviewing the list of Designated Persons and maintain a register of Designated Persons, and will notify relevant individuals of their inclusion on or removal from the register.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An executive outside section 4.2 today can be brought within it at the Managing Director's discretion, so any structure entered by a non-Designated employee should be documented to survive, or be unwound on, later designation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If it becomes apparent that a Director has breached this policy, APA Group will give careful consideration to whether it ought to make an announcement to the market explaining the circumstances of the breach and what, if any, remedial and/or disciplinary action it has taken.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach by a Director carries express reputational exposure through a possible market announcement, raising the stakes on any structure that sits close to the 4.2.5 line.

APA.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a Director or Designated Person under this policy. Section 4.2.5 prohibits them at any time, expressly including outside Closed Periods, from entering any hedging instrument or arrangement regarding, or any derivative financial product issued over, any APA Securities they hold, so both the purchased put and the written call are banned outright, whatever the vesting state of the shares and with no clearance route; the section 4.2.7 exceptional circumstances power relieves only against dealing during a Closed Period and does not touch section 4.2.5. The financing leg fails independently: APA Securities may be charged only as part of a diversified portfolio under a margin loan or secured financing arrangement whose terms do not permit title to the securities to be transferred, which excludes a loan secured solely on the collared parcel and any title-transfer or rehypothecation collateral, and unvested or holding-locked securities can never be charged at all. Charged securities remain subject to the policy, so a margin call or lender enforcement sale during a Closed Period needs exceptional circumstances permission from the Chairman rather than being an excluded dealing. These restrictions extend to Related Parties, and the Managing Director can add executives to the Designated Persons register at any time; only employees and contractors outside section 4.2 are unconstrained, and they are the wrong client for this product.

rules.detail: Express ban on any arrangement or transaction designed or intended to hedge or otherwise limit economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities, with approval expressly unavailable.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that: is designed or intended to hedge (or otherwise limit) your economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities (e.g. unvested employee share plan shares)

rules.detail: 'Restricted' Xero Securities are treated alongside unvested securities in the hedging ban, so vested shares still subject to a plan restriction or holding lock cannot be hedged. The policy does not say whether the 'approval will not be given' carve-out extends to restricted (as opposed to unvested) securities.
rules.evidence: is designed or intended to hedge (or otherwise limit) your economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities (e.g. unvested employee share plan shares)

rules.detail: Hedging vested unrestricted shares is caught twice: by the catch-all in the derivatives sentence ('any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities', which is not limited to unvested holdings) and by the ban on arrangements that enable you to profit from a decrease in the market price. Exceptional-circumstances approval is theoretically available for vested holdings.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that: ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly listed in the banned derivative products, so a prepaid forward or share swap is prohibited. A monetisation structured as a loan secured on Xero Securities is instead permitted with clearance under the secured financing paragraph.
rules.evidence: This includes OTC products, depository receipts, contracts for difference, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, exchange-traded options, caps and collars

rules.detail: Short selling is expressly included in the ban on short-term or speculative dealing, subject only to the exceptional-circumstances clearance route. Defined as borrowing and selling securities hoping to buy them back at a lower price.
rules.evidence: You must not deal in Xero Securities on a short term or speculative basis (including short selling), except in exceptional circumstances and with prior clearance to deal (see section 6).

rules.section: 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Stock lending is expressly permitted subject to prior clearance under the section 6 process, whether or not the person is a Designated Person. No conditions or price triggers are prescribed.
rules.evidence: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance (in accordance with the process in section 6) before you: ... enter into a transaction that amounts to stock lending of your Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are named in the list of prohibited derivative-market products.
rules.evidence: This includes OTC products, depository receipts, contracts for difference, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, exchange-traded options, caps and collars

rules.section: 6; 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Margin loans are permitted with prior clearance for everyone, Designated Person or not. Transferring existing Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account is expressly caught as a separate clearance trigger.
rules.evidence: you must seek clearance (in accordance with the process in section 6) before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account)

rules.section: 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Granting a security or rights over Xero Securities is permitted subject to prior clearance; the wording 'or rights' is wider than a formal charge and would capture a bank's control or set-off rights over collared shares. It is also a dealing under section 3 as a creation of an interest in Xero Securities.
rules.evidence: grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities

rules.section: 6; 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Secured financing is not banned. Any margin loan 'or other secured financing arrangement' requires prior clearance through the section 6 process, and section 6 confirms that even non-Designated Persons must obtain clearance for it. The policy imposes no vesting restriction on collateral and no ongoing disclosure obligation.
rules.evidence: you will need to seek clearance to deal in Xero Securities if you want to deal during a Xero Closed Period (in exceptional circumstances), enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, or grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Buy-sell window test: buying and selling listed securities within a 6 month period is short term dealing and is prohibited except in exceptional circumstances with prior clearance. Selling within 6 months of acquisition through vesting or exercise under an employee equity plan is carved out.
rules.evidence: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period. This can be a key indicator of insider trading, particularly if undertaken on a regular basis or in large amounts.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not engage in transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities. This includes OTC products ... caps and collars and any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that names 'collars' and 'OTC products' expressly, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited on their face rather than merely caught by a definition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances as the only derivatives gate
bespoke_clauses.clause: You may apply for approval to enter into one of these transactions in exceptional circumstances. Approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares is not absolutely barred, but it can only proceed through an exceptional-circumstances application (severe hardship, court order or similar), which a commercial monetisation is unlikely to satisfy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance ... before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account); grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan and security legs of a funded collar are permitted with clearance, so the structure fails only on the derivative legs; a plain secured loan against Xero shares without a hedge is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This limb is not restricted to unvested holdings and independently catches the purchased put in a collar over fully vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Xero takes a 'substance over form' approach and has regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring around the derivatives ban (for example a non-recourse loan with an economically equivalent payoff, or a hedge booked at a Connected Person entity) will be assessed on its economic substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where clearance is required to deal under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not meet the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the permitted secured financing leg can be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons being given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: They may also decide to impose conditions on the dealing or withdraw the clearance at any time. If your clearance is not approved or is withdrawn, you must keep this fact confidential. Clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to signing or drawdown; it can be withdrawn at any time or lapse automatically, and the executive cannot explain why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Your Connected Persons should only deal in Xero Securities in circumstances where you yourself would be permitted to do so. Where clearance requirements would apply to your dealing, you must comply with those requirements on behalf of your Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the derivatives ban or the clearance obligation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under six months, or one whose entry and physical settlement fall within six months, risks characterisation as short-term dealing on top of the derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no venue limitation and no vesting limitation on the derivatives ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike venue-limited bans elsewhere, this catch-all covers OTC bank-written puts and calls over on-market as well as plan-sourced shares.

XRO.summary: A funded collar is effectively not possible under this policy. The financing legs are workable: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, a grant of security or rights over Xero Securities, and stock lending are all permitted with prior clearance under section 6, for Designated Persons and non-Designated Persons alike, with no restriction on using vested shares as collateral and no ongoing financier disclosure regime. The derivative legs, however, are expressly prohibited: section 8 bans transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities and specifically names OTC products, forward contracts, swaps and 'caps and collars', together with any other product that limits economic risk or enables the holder to profit from a price decrease, and that catch-all is not limited to unvested holdings. The only route is an application for approval in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or a comparable individual circumstance), which cannot be given at all over unvested Xero Securities and would rarely be granted for a commercial monetisation; any approval must also pass the Front Page Test, can be conditioned or withdrawn at any time, and must be exercised within 5 business days. Even if approved, the trade would have to fall outside the 31 March and 30 September Closed Periods and any Board-set period, avoid the six-month short-term dealing window, and be notified to the Company Secretary on the day if the holder is a director.

Paragraph 3.45(a) then extends Dealing for Nominated Qantas Employees to prohibit any contract entered into with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to price fluctuations, which is exactly what the two collar legs do. The paragraph is not limited by vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For Nominated Qantas Employees, the definition of Dealing is further extended to prohibit: (a) hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas ...; and (b) any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single paragraph blocks both legs of a funded collar for directors and executives, and its drafting is ambiguous between a flat ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would leave both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside Closed Periods; the point should be settled with the Company Secretary before any structuring work.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing prohibition is qualified, so a facility in which the bank has no independent power of sale (for example, cash-settled legs, a non-recourse structure with no enforcement right over the shares, or security requiring the executive to direct any sale) may fall outside 3.45(b) even though a conventional margin loan does not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: set off and withholding rights are encumbrances
bespoke_clauses.clause: including a mortgage, charge, pledge, lien or title retention arrangement, right of set off or right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, or any third party interest such as a trust or an equity
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ordinary bank documentation terms such as set-off and the right to withhold a cash collateral deposit are themselves prohibited encumbrances, so even a lightly secured collar loan is caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given clearance to Deal as outlined in paragraphs 3.44 and 3.46, except in relation to Securities that are unvested
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unvested plan securities can never be hedged, pledged or dealt with, even in severe financial hardship, so the collateral and hedge pool is limited to vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this paragraph does not permit the Nominated Qantas Employee to otherwise Deal in those Restricted Securities

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval is valid for one month unless another period is agreed by the Chairman or CEO.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any exceptional-circumstances clearance gives a generous one-month execution window compared with the two to five business days common elsewhere, which would comfortably accommodate collar documentation and pricing if such a clearance could be obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “Securities” means shares, options or other securities or derivatives (including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, warrant or depository receipt) issued by any listed entity or issued or created over the listed entity's securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Bank-written OTC options over Qantas shares are Securities with no venue limitation, so entering the collar is a Dealing in its own right and not merely a hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any family member or associate over whom they have influence, including specifically any person who lives in the same home as the Nominated Qantas Employee
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a spouse, household member or influenced entity does not escape the paragraph 3.44 and 3.45 restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Nominated Qantas Employees means Directors, Company Secretaries, Executive Management Members, direct reports to Executive Management Members, and other Executives specifically notified by the CEO or his nominee from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Employees below direct reports to Executive Management Members are outside the hedging, margin lending and encumbrance prohibitions entirely and face only the statutory insider trading rule, but they are also unlikely to be the bank's target clients.

QAN.summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive of Qantas under this Code. Nominated Qantas Employees (directors, company secretaries, direct reports to the CEO and their direct reports, and anyone else the CEO nominates) have their Dealing definition extended by paragraph 3.45 to catch both legs of the structure: hedging or any contract entered into to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to the Qantas share price, and any margin lending, securities lending or grant of charge, lien, pledge, right of set off or third party interest over Qantas Securities where control of the sale process may be lost. Both limbs are unqualified as to vesting state, apply equally to influenced family members and household associates, and there is no clearance path expressed for them; the only relief, paragraph 3.48, is granted by the Chairman or CEO in exceptional circumstances such as severe hardship or a court order, is valid for one month, cannot touch unvested Securities and on its face releases only the paragraph 3.44 prohibition rather than 3.45. Two features are worth testing with the Company Secretary: the drafting of 3.45 is ambiguous between an outright ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would make both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside the 30 June and 31 December Closed Periods, and the financing limb is qualified by 'where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost', which a structure giving the bank no independent power of sale may not trigger. There is no short-term dealing rule, no minimum shareholding requirement and no financier disclosure obligation, so tenor and reporting are not obstacles; ordinary Qantas Employees below the Nominated tier are subject only to the statutory insider trading prohibition.

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading

bespoke_clauses.topic: collar named as restricted trading, not prohibited
bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into any other form of derivative contract relating to a security, such as a cap or collar facility; and any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: BlueScope names a collar facility in the list of what counts as trading rather than in a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are available to a Restricted Person inside a trading window with written clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: From the date this section takes effect, Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangements under which their BlueScope Steel securities are pledged as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This defeats the funded leg of a conventional collar loan, because a bank's security over the collared shares almost always includes an enforcement power of sale that does not require the holder's consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is conditional, so a facility with no independent power of sale (cash settlement only, or security requiring the executive to direct any disposal) may fall outside it, and this is the drafting point to negotiate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptions will not be considered in the case of trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a bank ever enforced, the executive would be in breach with no available cure, and breach is expressly a disciplinary matter that may include termination.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any dealing in the same BlueScope Steel securities within a 9 month period is prohibited
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: One of the longest short-term bans in the market: a collar over recently acquired shares, or one whose physical settlement occurs within nine months of the underlying purchase, would breach it, so tenor must exceed nine months and the underlying shares must be seasoned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the 45 day periods from the commencement of trading the day following the announcement of the half year results and the day following the announcement of the full year results; and the 15 day period from the commencement of the trading day following the Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Restricted Persons may deal only inside roughly 105 days a year, so collar entry, any roll and any physical settlement must all be scheduled into a window, and the Board may narrow a window before it opens.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ten trading day clearance with revocation
bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval to trade in BlueScope Steel securities is valid for 10 trading days from the time the approval is given, and may be revoked at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A comparatively long execution window for documenting and pricing a collar, but the bank cannot treat clearance as irrevocable up to signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if a genuine and pressing requirement for funds causes a need to sell BlueScope Steel securities, then exceptions may be considered
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is framed around a need to sell, so it is doubtful the Chairman could use it to authorise entry into a collar or a financing outside a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees who hold unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities must ... not enter any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedgeable pool is limited to shares that have vested and whose restriction period has ended; this ban applies to every employee, not only Restricted Persons, and has no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee or director must ensure that any Controlled Entity ... does not trade in BlueScope Steel securities except in accordance with this Policy (and as if the Controlled Entity itself was a Restricted Person).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A family trust or investment company used to hold the collared shares is treated as a Restricted Person in its own right, so the window, clearance and pledging rules follow the shares.

BSL.summary: A funded collar is close to workable at BlueScope but is defeated by the financing leg as ordinarily documented. The derivative legs are unusually accommodating: the policy names a 'cap or collar facility' and third party put and call options in the list of restricted trading rather than in a prohibition, so a Restricted Person may enter a collar over vested, unrestricted shares provided it is done inside one of the three trading windows (45 days after each of the half year and full year results, and 15 days after the AGM), after written notice to the Company Secretary, confirmation of no inside information and written clearance, which is valid for 10 trading days and revocable at any time. The loan leg is the problem: Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangement pledging BlueScope Steel securities as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale without the holder's consent, with no clearance route and no exemption authority, and any resulting forced sale is a breach for which exceptions will expressly not be considered. The prohibition is conditional rather than absolute, so a structure in which the bank has no independent power of sale over the collared shares is the only route worth exploring. Two further constraints apply: nothing may be hedged while unvested or within a restriction period, and the nine month short-term trading ban means the collar tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares must both exceed nine months.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging section is drafted as two targeted prohibitions rather than a general ban, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is left permitted and the derivative legs of a collar over those shares are available.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.2, 5.1, 5.3 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the most bank-friendly clause in the policy: enforcement by the lender, even in a blackout period, is expressly carved out of the short-term trading ban, the blackout and the notification and approval requirements, so the executive is not put in breach by the bank's own sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 5.6(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approving it, so the bank should expect the loan documentation to be negotiated with the Company Secretary rather than approved as presented.

bespoke_clauses.topic: directors notify rather than seek approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: a Director may deal at any time for a period of 5 business days following notification. By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors self-certify for ordinary dealings, giving a clean 5 business day execution window with no approval risk; note that this route does not extend to margin lending, which needs approval under section 5.6 regardless of tier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar that in substance hedges unvested or locked plan securities, even if written over an equal number of unrestricted shares, would be treated as breaching section 4.3, and a bespoke loan secured on shares should be cleared as if it were a margin lending arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy names only 'a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities' and 'transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account' as financing triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no general prohibition on granting security over Company securities and no financier disclosure regime, so the funding leg of a collar is unobstructed on the face of the policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forward contracts as short term dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar and of any forward element must exceed six months, and the collared shares should not have been bought on market within the preceding six months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities if ... the Company has notified Employees that they must not deal in securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-ended notice can be issued to all Employees at any time and would block collar entry, unwind or physical settlement without any stated end date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy refers throughout to 'the Company's securities' without defining the term and contains no derivatives or securities definition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is arguable that a bank-written OTC option is not itself one of 'the Company's securities', so the notification and approval regime may not formally bite on the derivative legs; the prudent course is to notify or clear them anyway given the substance over form clause.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A request for approval to deal will be answered as soon as practicable and typically within one business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unusually fast and explicit service level, which makes it practical to align clearance with pricing on a specific trade date.

WTC.summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at WiseTech, which is one of the more permissive policies in the market. Hedging is banned only for plan securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction, so vested unrestricted shares, including shares bought on market, may be hedged; the derivative legs would be a dealing requiring only prior notification to the Company Secretary and the Chair for a Director (with a 5 business day window and a same-day post-trade confirmation), or approval on a Clearance to Trade Request Form for other Restricted Persons, answered typically within one business day. The funding leg is likewise available: the only financing rule is that a margin lending arrangement, or a transfer of shares into an existing margin loan account, needs approval under section 5.5, and the Company may impose conditions on that approval, notably about when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call; there is no encumbrance ban, no vesting restriction on collateral and no financier disclosure obligation. Critically, section 6(e) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights as an Excluded Dealing outside the short-term trading ban, the blackout periods and the notification and approval requirements, so a bank enforcement sale does not put the executive in breach. The practical conditions are that entry falls outside the 30 June and 31 December blackout periods and any Board-specified or Company-notified dealing ban, that the tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares both exceed six months to avoid the short-term dealing rule, and that the structure is disclosed and cleared on a substance over form basis, since the Company can condition its approval on the enforcement mechanics of the loan.

MPL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any extension to a closed period and any additional period, which then form part of the defined Blackout Periods. The policy does not say whether such an extension or additional period is announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Section 6.3(b) is a standing ban on dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and section 6.4 defines those to include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties. There is no venue limit, so a bank-written OTC put and call are squarely caught, and the ban is not conditioned on the vesting state of any underlying shares. The only escape is 'the type of dealing permitted under this policy', which means the section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Employee must not: ... deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Medibank shares are equally caught by 6.3(b), and are independently Medibank Securities because their value is materially determined by reference to Medibank.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this section, financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: The scope clause confines sections 4 to 9, including the section 6 further restrictions, to Restricted Employees. An Employee outside the register is bound only by the insider trading prohibition and the confidentiality obligation, plus the hortatory 6.2(a) statement about short term and speculative trading.
rules.evidence: section 3 (insider trading) and section 10 (confidential information) apply to everyone (including all Employees, contractors and agents of Medibank); sections 3 to 7 (share trading policy), section 8 (process for trading) and section 9 (associates) apply to all Restricted Employees

rules.detail: Remuneration-based hedging ban expressed at the widest level: any transaction or arrangement with anyone which could have the effect of limiting risk exposure to unvested remuneration. No consent route and, because section 7.1(b) relief is limited to disposals, no exceptional-circumstances route either.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Employee must not: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested

rules.detail: Vested remuneration that remains subject to a holding lock is treated identically to unvested remuneration for hedging purposes.
rules.evidence: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The remuneration limb in 6.3(a) stops at holding-locked shares, but 6.3(b) independently bans dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and any hedge of vested unrestricted shares must be executed through such a product. Shares bought on market are therefore no more hedgeable than plan shares.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly in the 6.4 list of financial products, so a prepaid forward, forward sale or share swap over Medibank shares is prohibited. A monetisation structured purely as a secured loan without a derivative is instead permitted with Company Secretary consent under 6.1(b).
rules.evidence: financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Flat ban with no approval route, footnoted by reference to ASIC Regulatory Guide 196 and defined as selling financial products you do not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees are not permitted to engage in short selling of Medibank Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned. It is not a financial product under 6.4, not a funding arrangement with Medibank Securities as security under 6.1(b), and not within the description of dealing.

Contracts for difference are named in the 6.4 definition of financial products, so they fall within the standing 6.3(b) prohibition; a short CFD would also breach the short selling ban and, if closed within 90 days, the minimum holding period.
rules.evidence: derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties

rules.detail: Absolute ban with no consent route, expressly justified by the risk that the facility terms may force a sale during a Blackout Period or while the holder has Inside Information. The Relevant Notification Officer is the arbiter of whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement, which matters because the borderline with a 6.1(b) consented facility is where a collar loan sits.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Medibank Securities as the terms may require Medibank Securities to be sold during a Blackout Period or when the Restricted Employee possesses Inside Information.

rules.detail: Granting security over Medibank Securities is permitted with the consent of the Company Secretary. The clause is drafted so broadly that even an incidental 'all assets' security interest that happens to catch Medibank shares requires consent. No form, deadline, validity period or criteria for consent are specified.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must not, without the consent of the Company Secretary, enter into any other funding arrangements where Medibank Securities may be included as security (for example any lending arrangement that involves the Restricted Employee granting an 'all assets' security interest to secure the repayment of a loan).

rules.detail: Secured financing other than margin lending is available with Company Secretary consent, and a lender's enforcement sale under a consented facility is a Permitted Dealing excluded from the Blackout Periods and the notification process. The carve-out is expressly withheld for margin lending agreements and other funding arrangements prohibited by the policy, so the consent is what makes lender enforcement safe.
rules.evidence: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy

rules.detail: Hard 90 day minimum holding period applying to Medibank Securities and, notably, to financial products associated with Medibank Securities, so any derivative position would itself have to be held for at least 90 days. Securities granted under an employee incentive scheme are deemed held from the date of grant, which shortens the wait after vesting.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must hold any Medibank Securities or financial products associated with Medibank Securities for at least 90 days.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance, but the stated rationale for the margin lending ban is that 'the terms may require Medibank Securities to be sold during a Blackout Period or when the Restricted Employee possesses Inside Information'. A facility whose terms cannot force a sale on a price trigger is therefore materially easier to characterise as a consentable 6.1(b) funding arrangement rather than a prohibited margin lending arrangement, and the Relevant Notification Officer is expressly the arbiter of that classification.

MPL.exemption_authority: The Relevant Notification Officer may give prior confirmation, in exceptional circumstances, for a Restricted Employee to deal during a Blackout Period, or to dispose of Medibank Securities even if otherwise prohibited under section 6. Exceptional circumstances may include severe financial hardship, court orders or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements, or other circumstances determined by the Chair of the Board (or Chair of the Audit Committee where the Chair of the Board is involved); the discretion must be exercised with caution where there is doubt, and the dealing must be confirmed in writing within three business days. Crucially the section 7.1(b) relief is limited to disposals, so it cannot authorise entry into a hedge, derivative or financing that section 6 prohibits. Separately, the Company Secretary may consent under 6.1(b) to a funding arrangement secured on Medibank Securities.
