bespoke_clauses.topic: standing ban on all associated financial products
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Employee must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: it is unqualified as to vesting state and venue, and the only carve-out is the closed list of section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purposes of this section, financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Third-party created OTC instruments are expressly within scope, so a bank-written put and call over Medibank shares cannot be argued outside the prohibition on the basis that they are not exchange traded.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition, Restricted Employees must not, without the consent of the Company Secretary, enter into any other funding arrangements where Medibank Securities may be included as security (for example any lending arrangement that involves the Restricted Employee granting an 'all assets' security interest to secure the repayment of a loan).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funding leg of a collar is available with Company Secretary consent, so a plain loan secured on Medibank shares is possible even though the hedge is not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: consented lender enforcement is a permitted dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by a bank under a facility consented to under 6.1(b) is excluded from the Blackout Periods and the notification process, but enforcement under any facility the policy prohibits is not protected, which makes obtaining the Company Secretary's consent the single most important condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees should consult the Relevant Notification Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Whether a collar loan is a prohibited margin lending arrangement or a consentable 6.1(b) funding arrangement is decided by the company, not the bank, so the classification should be confirmed in writing before the facility is documented.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Employee may request, and the Relevant Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Restricted Employee to: (a) deal in Medibank Securities during a Blackout Period; or (b) dispose of Medibank Securities even if otherwise prohibited under section 6
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only relief from section 6 is a disposal, so no exceptional circumstance, however severe, can authorise entering a hedge, derivative or prohibited financing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ninety day hold applies to the derivative itself
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees must hold any Medibank Securities or financial products associated with Medibank Securities for at least 90 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the derivative ban were relaxed, the collar position itself would have to be held for at least 90 days, ruling out short-dated or early-terminable structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Medibank Securities" means Securities of, or whose value is materially determined by reference to, Medibank.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Instruments whose value tracks the Medibank share price are Medibank Securities in their own right, so the clearance, blackout and 90 day holding rules attach to them directly and not only through the section 6 prohibition; note the general Securities definition is limited to products 'able to be traded on a financial market', a tension the section 6.4 definition overrides for section 6 purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: companies with which the Restricted Employee is connected by directly or indirectly: (i) holding at least 20% of the share capital; or (ii) controlling the exercise of at least 20% of the voting power ... a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Restricted Employee or his or her spouse, partner or child or step-child under the age of 18
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A 20% shareholding threshold and any family trust are enough to make a counterparty entity an Associate, so booking the collar or the loan away from the individual does not avoid the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance expires five (5) business days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date. ... Restricted Employees must confirm in writing to the Relevant Notification Officer, within three (3) business days of the dealing in Medibank Securities, the number of Medibank Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted leg must be executed within 5 business days of clearance and the bank's identity as counterparty must be disclosed to the company within 3 business days, since 'the relevant parties to the dealing' must be reported.

MPL.summary: A funded collar is not available to a Medibank director or executive, because the hedge is prohibited even though the loan is not. Section 6.3(b) bans a Restricted Employee from dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and section 6.4 defines those to include derivatives, options, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties, with no venue limit and no vesting qualification; the only carve-out is the closed list of section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative, and the section 7 exceptional-circumstances relief from section 6 extends only to disposals, so no hardship application can authorise entry into a collar. The funding leg by contrast is workable: margin lending is banned outright, but section 6.1(b) permits any other funding arrangement in which Medibank Securities may be included as security with the consent of the Company Secretary, and section 5(e) then treats a disposal resulting from that lender exercising its rights as a Permitted Dealing outside the Blackout Periods, provided the facility is a consented one rather than a prohibited margin lending arrangement. A bank should therefore expect to be able to offer a secured loan against vested Medibank shares, subject to written Company Secretary consent and to confirming with the Relevant Notification Officer that the facility is not classified as margin lending, but not the put and call legs. Any permitted dealing must also fall outside the 1 January and 1 July Blackout Periods and any Board-specified extension, be cleared in advance by the applicable Relevant Notification Officer within a 5 business day clearance window, be confirmed in writing within 3 business days identifying the counterparty, and respect the 90 day minimum holding period, which applies to associated financial products as well as to shares.

MIN.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All Directors, officers, employees and contractors of the Company and its subsidiaries, and any other person notified that the Policy applies to them. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the Closed Period bar, the Front Page Test and the excluded trading list, but not by the clearance, short-term, hedging or secured financing rules.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, members of the MinRes Senior Leadership Team (Executive General Manager role or above, including the Company Secretary), and any other person advised in writing by the Company Secretary (which may be ad hoc, e.g. staff working on a market sensitive matter). Subject to prior written clearance, ad hoc trading prohibitions, the short-term and speculative trading ban, and the hedging and secured financing rules.

MIN.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose further restrictions on Designated Persons dealing in MinRes securities or securities of other companies by notifying them in writing; additional prohibited periods are imposed when the Company is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. The Company Secretary may also designate additional persons as Designated Persons in writing on an ad hoc basis. Refusal of clearance or revocation of an approval must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Dealing' extends to creating a derivative over securities and to entering into an agreement to do so, and 'securities' means Division 3 financial products including derivatives, with no venue limit, so an OTC put and call with a bank is a dealing requiring prior written clearance from the Clearance Officer and is barred in Closed Periods. The Closed Period bar separately names 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities'.
rules.evidence: It also extends to subscribing for new securities, exercising options over securities and creating a derivative over securities and includes entering into an agreement to do any of those things

rules.detail: Personnel who are not Designated Persons need no clearance, but must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of MinRes securities during a Closed Period, and may never deal while holding Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not deal in the Company's securities, or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, during a Closed Period (unless exceptional circumstances apply).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any arrangement limiting a KMP's exposure to risk on unvested remuneration. Extends to the KMP's Connected Parties.
rules.evidence: A member of the Company's key management personnel, or a Connected Party of such a member, must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The same absolute ban expressly captures remuneration that has vested but 'remains subject to a holding lock', so a collar over holding-locked shares is unavailable to KMP even with approval.
rules.evidence: an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The KMP ban is confined to unvested or holding-locked remuneration and so does not reach freely held vested shares. The approval-gated bullets are addressed to 'Other Designated Persons', leaving it unclear whether they bind KMP; the prudent reading, and the one the Front Page Test supports, is that a KMP hedging vested unrestricted shares needs the same prior written approval from the Clearance Officer.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Persons must not: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company ... unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.

No security-state distinction is drawn for this tier, and the excluded trading list contemplates a secured lender later selling under such an approved arrangement.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Persons must not: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company; or use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.

rules.detail: The hedging section binds only key management personnel and Designated Persons; Personnel below that level are not addressed, subject only to the insider trading, Closed Period and Front Page Test constraints.

rules.section: Hedging and secured financing arrangements; Definitions (dealing)

rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company

rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on ... a speculative basis (including short selling).

Granting security is not itself within the definition of dealing, so the approval requirement, not the clearance regime, is the operative gate; the excluded trading list then protects the lender's later enforcement sale.
rules.evidence: or use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer

bespoke_clauses.clause: Other Designated Persons must not ... use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one does not ban secured financing outright but gates it on a single prior written approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is available in principle to Directors and other Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: lender disposals – a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights where prior written approval was received for entry into the arrangement, is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement or physical settlement sale is excluded from the Policy, including during a Closed Period, provided the collar and loan were approved up front, which removes the usual fatal forced-sale risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A member of the Company's key management personnel, or a Connected Party of such a member, must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For KMP the collar can only be written over shares that have both vested and come off any holding lock, and no approval can cure a collar over unvested or locked remuneration.

bespoke_clauses.topic: drafting gap for KMP on vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval-gated bullets on limiting economic risk and using securities as loan security are addressed to 'Other Designated Persons', while the preceding paragraph addresses key management personnel only in respect of unvested or holding-locked remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express rule permitting or prohibiting a KMP hedging or pledging fully vested unrestricted shares, so a bank should require the Clearance Officer's written approval and, ideally, a Board confirmation of the reading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on ... a speculative basis (including short selling).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A written call and purchased put must be documented as risk management over a long-held position rather than a speculative or short position, and the collar should be delta-neutral rather than net short.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a short-term basis (ie buying and selling within 3 months)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar tenor and any unwind or roll should sit outside a three-month buy-and-sell pattern in the underlying shares, and shares recently acquired should not be collared and delivered within three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Periods run from the end of the financial year, half year, September quarter and March quarter until the first trading day after release of the corresponding results or quarterly report.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: MinRes has four blackouts a year because of quarterly reporting, so the windows for pricing and executing the collar and any roll are materially narrower than at a half-yearly reporter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Clearance Officer ... may revoke their approval at any time. An approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar must complete inside five business days of clearance, and the bank bears the risk that clearance is revoked before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Clearance Officer ... may in their discretion grant or refuse the request, or impose conditions on the dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may come with conditions such as tenor, strike levels, disclosure or a maximum proportion of the holding, which must be capable of being reflected in the confirmation and loan documents.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings that would not satisfy the Front Page Test should not occur, even where the dealing may not strictly be prohibited under this Policy or otherwise at law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An anti-avoidance overlay that can defeat a technically compliant collar on reputational grounds, so the structure should be capable of clean public description and, for Directors, of Appendix 3Y disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel must not deal in the Company's securities, or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, during a Closed Period (unless exceptional circumstances apply).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, unwind, roll and cash settlement of the OTC options are themselves barred in Closed Periods for everyone, not just Designated Persons, absent an exceptional-circumstances approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Parties only deal in securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or superannuation fund does not avoid the approval and clearance requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must immediately notify the Company Secretary of any dealings in the Company's securities when any such dealings occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary immediately and, for Directors, will feed a Listing Rule 3.19A Appendix 3Y disclosure of the change in the nature of their interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: pre-determined investment or divestment plans – dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided by the Board and ... the plan cannot be cancelled during a Closed Period except in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers an alternative route: physical settlement of the collar could be structured as a Board-cleared non-discretionary plan so settlement is not blocked by a Closed Period.

MIN.summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at MinRes, which is unusual. The Policy does not ban secured financing or hedging outright: 'Other Designated Persons' may both limit the economic risk of their MinRes holding and use MinRes securities as security for loans, expressly including hedging and margin loan arrangements, provided prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, Chair of the Board for other Directors, Managing Director for everyone else), and the excluded trading list then protects the bank's enforcement sale by carving out a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights where that prior approval was obtained. The hard limits are that key management personnel and their Connected Parties can never hedge remuneration that is unvested or subject to a holding lock, so the collar must be written only over shares that have vested and come off any lock, and the derivative legs are themselves dealings requiring clearance, executed within five business days, outside the four annual Closed Periods (financial year, half year, September and March quarters) and any Listing Rule 3.1A blackout. The structure must not look speculative or short, should avoid a three-month buy-and-sell pattern, must survive the Front Page Test, and must be notified to the Company Secretary immediately (with Appendix 3Y disclosure for Directors). A drafting gap leaves it unclear whether the approval-gated bullets bind KMP in respect of fully vested unrestricted shares, so a bank should insist on written Clearance Officer approval covering both the derivative legs and the security in every case.

MEZ.title: Trading In Securities Policy

tiers.name: Meridian Persons
tiers.description: Directors and employees of, and contractors and secondees to, Meridian or any of Meridian's subsidiaries. Subject to the three general rules: no insider trading, no short term trading without General Counsel approval, and no transactions in Associated Products. No trading approval or blackout regime applies to this tier.

tiers.name: Meridian Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors of Meridian; the Chief Executive, all members of the Executive Management Team and their direct reports; all legal and investor relations staff; all staff who are members of the Long Term Incentive Plan; during a buyback, those involved in or with knowledge of it; and anyone else notified by the General Counsel. Subject to five additional rules: holdings disclosure, the Blackout Period ban, prior General Counsel approval for all trading, post-trade notification, and the margin loan prohibition. They remain deemed Meridian Restricted Persons for six months after departure.

tiers.name: all directors of Meridian
tiers.description: Distinguished for approval mechanics (the approval form must be countersigned by the Chair, or for the Chair by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) and for post-trade notification feeding the ASX Appendix 3Y and concurrent NZX lodgement.

tiers.name: the Chief Executive, all members of the Executive Management Team and their direct reports
tiers.description: Senior executive tier within Meridian Restricted Persons. The Chief Executive's approval form must be countersigned by the Chair or Deputy Chair; the Chief Executive and their direct reports also have NZ statutory relevant-interest disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: all staff who are members of the Long Term Incentive Plan
tiers.description: Plan membership alone makes a person a Meridian Restricted Person, so every LTI participant is inside the approval, blackout and margin loan regime as well as the Associated Products ban.

tiers.name: companies, trusts and other entities controlled by any Meridian Person and any family member or other person acting on the direction or recommendation of a Meridian Person
tiers.description: The Policy applies directly to these persons and entities, not merely by requiring the Meridian Person to procure their compliance. The margin loan ban is expressly extended to holdings in the name of spouses, partners or dependent children, trusts of which the person is trustee, and any company the person controls.

MEZ.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Meridian's General Counsel may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time in relation to Meridian Securities, and any period in relation to specified Other Financial Products, either generally for all Meridian Restricted Persons or in relation to specified Meridian Restricted Persons. The General Counsel may also notify additional persons as Meridian Restricted Persons by name, designation, position or business group. The Policy does not say whether such periods or notifications are confidential.

rules.section: What this policy applies to; Additional Rules Two and Three
rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Meridian Securities' expressly includes options or derivatives in respect of any securities of Meridian, and the exchange-traded qualifier attaches only to the residual limb 'any other financial product that is traded on a financial market', so an OTC put and call over Meridian shares is a Meridian Security. Trading in it therefore needs prior written General Counsel approval and is barred in Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: any other securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries, including any debentures, convertible notes, units of shares, options or derivatives (including futures contracts listed on a futures exchange) in respect of any securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries and any other financial product that is traded on a financial market.

rules.section: Rules applicable to all Meridian Persons
rules.detail: Meridian Persons who are not Restricted Persons need no approval and are not subject to Blackout Periods; they are constrained only by the insider trading ban, the three-month short term trading rule and, if they participate in an equity-based remuneration scheme, the Associated Products ban.
rules.evidence: Meridian's trading in securities policy consists of: Three rules applicable to all Meridian Persons; Five additional rules applicable to Meridian Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any product limiting the economic risk of participating in an entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme. It binds every Meridian Person entitled to participate in such a scheme, and so covers all LTI participants and all Restricted Persons who hold plan entitlements.
rules.evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Rule Three is drafted around 'participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme' rather than around vesting, so shares that have vested but remain held under the scheme or subject to a restriction are still an entitlement under it and cannot be hedged. The Policy nowhere uses the language of vesting or holding locks.
rules.evidence: any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme

rules.detail: Once scheme shares have vested and been delivered free of restriction they arguably cease to be an 'entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme', taking them outside Rule Three; the same is true of shares bought on market. A collar over such shares is still a trade in Meridian Securities requiring prior written General Counsel approval, outside a Blackout Period. The boundary is untested on the face of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Before trading in Meridian Securities outside of a Blackout Period ... Meridian Restricted Persons must, using the form at the back of this policy: seek approval from the General Counsel

rules.detail: For a Meridian Person who is not a Restricted Person, hedging shares that are no longer an entitlement under a remuneration scheme is not prohibited and requires no approval, subject only to the insider trading ban.
rules.evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'.

rules.section: Rule One ('Trade'); Additional Rules Three and Five
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of Meridian Securities and so a trade needing General Counsel approval; if it is monetised by a loan secured on Meridian Securities it is separately caught by the Additional Rule Five ban, and if it monetises a scheme entitlement it is an Associated Product.
rules.evidence: 'Trade' includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or other financial products, or agreeing to do so.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy, and there is no speculative trading ban. A short sale would still be a disposal of Meridian Securities and so a trade requiring General Counsel approval for a Restricted Person.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of 'Trade', which reaches only applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or agreeing to do so.

rules.section: What this policy applies to; Additional Rule Three
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over Meridian shares is a derivative in respect of securities of Meridian and so a Meridian Security, making it a trade requiring prior General Counsel approval; there is no speculative trading ban to bar it outright, but a CFD position opened and closed within three months would breach Rule Two.
rules.evidence: options or derivatives (including futures contracts listed on a futures exchange) in respect of any securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval route, expressly retrospective ('or continue with'), covering both loans to fund acquisition of Meridian Securities and loans in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as security. Extended to holdings in the name of spouses, partners, dependent children, trusts where the person is trustee, and controlled companies.
rules.evidence: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Additional Rule Five binds only Meridian Restricted Persons; the Policy is silent on margin loans by other Meridian Persons.

Granting security over Meridian Securities is not itself a 'Trade', but the second limb of Additional Rule Five bans any arrangement 'in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan'. The noun in the sentence is 'margin loan arrangements', so a purist could argue a bespoke bank facility is outside it, but the second limb and the stated rationale (forced sale in a Blackout Period) point the other way.
rules.evidence: any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan

rules.detail: No encumbrance or pledge rule applies to Meridian Persons outside the Restricted Person population, and granting security is not a 'Trade'.

The loan leg of a funded collar is a loan in relation to which Meridian Securities are used as security against repayment, which Additional Rule Five prohibits for every Restricted Person, including through a spouse, dependent child, trust or controlled company, with no approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route. The General Counsel's exceptional-circumstances discretion is expressed only in relation to Blackout Period trading, not Rule Five.
rules.evidence: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.

rules.detail: Secured financing is regulated only through Additional Rule Five, which applies to Meridian Restricted Persons alone.

Acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within three months is banned for everyone, subject only to advance General Counsel approval in exceptional circumstances. There is no carve-out for shares acquired on vesting under an incentive plan.
rules.evidence: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved in advance by Meridian's General Counsel.

clearance.approver: General Counsel (on the form at the back of the Policy)
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than two business days after completion of the trade

bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The second limb catches any loan secured on Meridian Securities, so the funded leg of a collar is prohibited for every director, executive and LTI participant, with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not merely prospective, so an existing secured facility must be unwound rather than grandfathered, and a person becoming a Restricted Person must exit any such arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction applies whether the Meridian Securities are held: in the name of the Meridian Restricted Person; or in the name of their spouses or partners or dependent children; or by trusts of which the Meridian Restricted Person is a trustee; or by any company which a Meridian Restricted Person controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the secured borrowing through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product' ... any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An absolute, approval-proof ban on the option legs to the extent they hedge scheme entitlements; it turns on eligibility under the scheme rather than on vesting, so the safest collar covers only shares acquired independently of any plan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Restricted Persons remain subject to this policy and will be deemed to be Meridian Restricted Persons for six months after their departure from Meridian.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A retiring director or executive cannot put on a funded collar for six months after leaving, so the bank must diligence departure dates rather than current office.

bespoke_clauses.topic: loan itself may be a security
bespoke_clauses.clause: Security is defined broadly and includes any interest in, or right to participate in, any capital, assets, earnings, royalties, or other property of any person, and any interest in, or right to be paid, money that is, or is to be deposited with, lent to, or otherwise owing by, any person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On its face the definition sweeps in debt claims, so the loan and the OTC option confirmations could themselves be characterised as securities under the Policy, reinforcing that every leg needs General Counsel approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: must complete the approved trade within 10 trading days from the date of notification ... trading is still prohibited if a Meridian Restricted Person who has secured approval either has, or learns of, material information which is not generally available to the market. In those circumstances, the approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the option legs must complete within 10 trading days (2 trading days if approved for a Blackout Period), and the approval evaporates automatically if material information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of proposed trading by a director or the Chief Executive, the form must be signed by the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair and in the case of proposed trading by the Chair, the form must be signed by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Board-level sign-off, not merely a General Counsel tick, is needed before a director or the Chief Executive can execute any leg, which lengthens the lead time inside the 10 trading day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that Meridian's General Counsel specifies from time to time in relation to Meridian Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can be imposed on all or specified Restricted Persons at any time, blocking entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement of the structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no incentive plan carve-out from short term rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most policies there is no exemption for selling shares received on vesting, so shares acquired within three months should not be delivered into a collar settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It also applies to companies, trusts and other entities controlled by any Meridian Person and any family member or other person acting on the direction or recommendation of a Meridian Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The counterparty to the collar cannot be a family trust or controlled entity used to sidestep the approval and margin loan rules, as those entities are themselves bound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Meridian's objection is to lender-driven forced sales, so an unfunded collar with cash settlement and no security interest is the structure most likely to be approvable; the Policy contains no forced-sale carve-out.

MEZ.summary: A funded collar is not available to any Meridian director, executive or LTI participant. Additional Rule Five bans Meridian Restricted Persons from entering into or continuing with any loan arrangement in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as security against repayment, expressly extending to spouses, dependent children, trusts and controlled companies, and there is no approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route out of it; the General Counsel's discretion reaches only Blackout Period and short term trading. The option legs are separately constrained: an OTC put and call over Meridian shares is a Meridian Security, so a Restricted Person needs prior written General Counsel approval on the prescribed form (countersigned by the Chair for directors and the Chief Executive), executed within 10 trading days, outside the 31 May and 30 November Blackout Periods and any period the General Counsel specifies. Rule Three separately bans, with no approval route and for all Meridian Persons, any product limiting the economic risk of an entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme, so the collar could in no event be written over plan entitlements. At most an unfunded, unsecured, cash-settled collar over independently acquired shares held for more than three months might be approved, and even that binds a departing executive for six months after they leave.

RHC.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: The directors of the Company and all employees of the Group in all regions in which the Group operates directly or via joint venture. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, confidentiality, the Front Page Test and the ban on dealing in other companies' securities, but not by the blackout, approval, short-term, margin loan or hedging rules.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All key management personnel of the Company (including directors), as well as other persons who are likely to possess Inside Information regarding the Company; the Procedures give further guidance on who qualifies. Subject to blackout periods, prior approval for every dealing, the 12-month short-term and short-selling bans, the margin loan and encumbrance approval requirement, the hedging approval requirement and post-trade confirmation.

RHC.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (section 5.1). Separately, the Company may notify Employees that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until further notice (section 4.1). The Policy does not state whether such periods are announced or confidential, but a refusal or withdrawal of approval must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: There is no separate derivatives rule, but 'dealing' is defined to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products available in connection with the Company's securities, with an express substance over form approach and no venue limit. An OTC put and call is therefore a dealing needing prior written approval under section 5.4, and a hedging approval under 5.8, and is barred in blackout periods.
rules.evidence: When the expression 'deal' or 'dealing' is used in this Policy, it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities. ... The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.

rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons are subject only to the insider trading prohibition, any Company notice not to deal, and the Front Page Test; sections 5.1 to 5.8 do not apply to them.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons.

rules.detail: Hedging Company securities is permitted with prior written approval, sought from the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary and determined by the relevant Approving Officer under section 5.5. There is no outright ban and no security-state limitation in the operative words.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.

rules.detail: Unusually, the Policy does not absolutely prohibit hedging unvested plan securities; it gives that as the illustration of what counts as hedging and subjects it to the same prior written approval. Approval would still have to survive the Front Page Test and the terms of the relevant equity plan, which are outside the Policy.
rules.evidence: for example, entering into arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to a staff or director equity plan

rules.detail: Section 5.8 binds only Restricted Persons and Connected Persons; hedging by other Employees is not addressed.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan limits the economic risk associated with holding Company securities and so needs hedging approval, and if secured it also needs approval under 5.7. The tension is section 5.2, which names forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing, so a monetisation structure must be long-dated to avoid that ban.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval route, defined by reference to borrowing a security and selling it to buy back lower. The exceptional-circumstances relief in 5.3 covers only blackout and short-term dealing, not short selling.
rules.evidence: Short sell the Company's securities. Short selling refers to the practice of borrowing a security and selling it in the hope that it can be bought back at a lower price at some time in the future to close out the short position.

rules.detail: The short-selling ban in section 5.2 is addressed only to Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

Securities lending arrangements are named in the chapeau to 5.7 and any dealing in connection with one requires prior written approval, treated under the section 5.5 process. Lending stock to facilitate a short position would still run into the 5.2 short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product available in connection with the Company's securities and so a dealing requiring approval, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling ban and a CFD closed within 12 months would breach the short-term dealing ban, so approval is unlikely.
rules.evidence: it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling securities to satisfy a margin call each require prior written approval under the section 5.5 process.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan

The grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over Company securities is expressly listed as requiring prior written approval, not prohibited. The bullet is general in terms even though the chapeau frames 5.7 around margin lending and securities lending arrangements.

rules.detail: No encumbrance rule applies to Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons.

Secured financing over Company securities is permitted with prior written approval: the encumbrance bullet in 5.7(a) covers any mortgage, charge, lien, encumbrance or third party interest, and the Policy then carves the lender's enforcement sale out of the blackout, short-term and approval rules. Section 6 does not disapply 5.7 or 5.8, so approval for the arrangement itself is always needed.

rules.detail: Secured financing is regulated only through section 5.7, which binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

A twelve-month rule, far longer than the market-standard three months, and it reaches beyond on-market round trips to 'other short-term dealings', with forward contracts given as the example. Relief is available only on an exceptional-circumstances application under 5.3 (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order). Participation in an equity plan is excluded from 5.2, but dealing in plan securities once they cease to be held under the plan is not.

RHC.exemption_authority: The Approving Officer for the applicant (Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chair; the Chair for other Directors; the Managing Director or Group CFO for other Restricted Persons) may approve dealing in a blackout period or on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances, and grants the margin loan, encumbrance and hedging approvals. bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement, including ... the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ramsay gates rather than bans secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar and the security over the collared shares are both available on a single prior written approval from the Approving Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is excluded from the blackout, short-term and pre-approval rules, so lender enforcement does not put the executive in breach; the carve-out is not limited to margin lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permitted on approval rather than banned, and the Policy does not carve unvested plan securities out of that approval route, which is unusually permissive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The single biggest constraint on tenor: the collar should run well beyond 12 months and should not be documented as, or economically equivalent to, a short-dated forward, since forward contracts are the Policy's own example of a prohibited short-term dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to: ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The excluded dealings list is expressed only against the blackout, short-term and pre-approval sections, so the margin loan, encumbrance and hedging approvals in 5.7 and 5.8 continue to apply to everything, including plan dealings and non-discretionary plans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar cannot be documented around the rules; if its economic effect is a short position, a short-dated forward or an unapproved hedge, it will be treated as one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express reputational veto over the hedging and secured financing approvals, so the structure must be capable of clean public description and Appendix 3Y-style disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the duration of the approval will be 5 business days ... The approval to deal can be withdrawn at any time by the Approving Officer in his/her absolute discretion without giving any reason ... it is recommended that Restricted Persons apply for approval to deal at least 2 business days prior to the intended date of dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, with two business days of lead time, and the bank bears the risk of unexplained withdrawal before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approving Officer may direct the person who is proposing to deal in the Company's securities not to deal, or impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may carry unexplained conditions on tenor, size, strikes or disclosure that the confirmation and loan documents must accommodate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Procedures provide further guidance around who is a Restricted Person and a Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The perimeter of the approval regime, and who counts as a Connected Person for a family trust or controlled company, is set by an internal document the bank has not seen and should request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan requires prior written approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A voluntary sale by the executive to meet a call needs fresh approval and may fall in a blackout, whereas a sale by the lender exercising its rights is excluded, so the facility should rely on lender enforcement rather than borrower top-up sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forfeiture of plan securities is an express sanction, which would strip collateral out of the structure if the arrangement is later found non-compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee or a Connected Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee or a Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers a route for physical settlement of the collar to occur without regard to blackout periods, if the settlement mechanics are pre-approved as a non-discretionary plan.

RHC.summary: A funded collar is achievable at Ramsay, subject to approvals and tenor. The Policy bans neither hedging nor secured financing: section 5.8 permits a Restricted Person or Connected Person to hedge Company securities with prior written approval, and section 5.7 permits the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over Company securities, and entry into margin lending arrangements, on the same approval. Approval is given by the Chair for directors, the Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chair, and the Managing Director or Group CFO for other Restricted Persons, lasts only five business days, may be withdrawn at any time without reasons, may carry undisclosed conditions and will be refused if the dealing fails the Front Page Test; entry must be outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any Board-specified period, and must be notified to the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary the same day. The critical constraint is section 5.2: short-term dealing covers a 12-month buy-and-sell window and expressly includes 'other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts)', so the collar must be long-dated and not economically a short-dated forward, and it must never be a short position. Helpfully, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the blackout, short-term and pre-approval rules, so the bank's enforcement sale does not breach the Policy, though the approvals in 5.7 and 5.8 are never disapplied by the section 6 exclusions.

ALQ.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, employees, consultants, contractors and advisors of the Company and its related bodies corporate. Bound by the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the Derivatives and Hedging rules; those who are not Designated Personnel may Trade at any time provided they hold no Inside Information.

tiers.name: Designated Personnel
tiers.description: Company Personnel who by seniority or position are likely to become involved with key financial, operational and strategic price-sensitive information: Directors, executives in regional management positions and above, financial professionals involved in preparing statutory accounts, and all head office corporate personnel. The Managing Director may add others. Confined to Approved Trading Periods and subject to the notice, margin loan, speculative trading and short selling bans.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, a subset of Designated Personnel, distinguished only for the notice regime (a director informs the Chair; the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee) and for the notifiable interest disclosure to the Company Secretary within 2 business days.

All rules of the policy apply to them and Company Personnel must ensure they abide by it.

The Board may only add further Approved Trading Periods ('any other period as determined by the Board from time to time'), and the Managing Director may determine additional officers or persons to whom the policy applies, which can bring a person within the Approved Trading Period regime.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no venue limit and no approval route, on any use of Derivatives over unvested Equity Interests by Company Personnel holding them and by their Connected Persons. Derivatives is defined to include put and call options and 'caps and collars', so a collar over unvested shares, options or performance rights is squarely caught.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel may use Derivatives, including OTC puts, calls and collars, over vested Company Securities subject only to the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the balance of the policy. No notice or approval is required of them.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Securities are expressly allowed, but for Designated Personnel entry into the derivative is Trading that must occur inside an Approved Trading Period and requires prior approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, plus written confirmation to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Personnel of the Company must seek approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade.

rules.detail: A director may enter a Derivative over vested Securities in an Approved Trading Period after informing the Chair (the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee); no approval is required, only prior notice, followed by written advice to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for ASX notification within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: A director of the Company must inform the Chair prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade;

rules.detail: The rationale given is that hedging unvested equity would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met and would break the connection between staff performance and shareholder interests. 'Any other hedging or investment arrangement' falls within the defined term Derivatives, so the ban is not limited to listed instruments.
rules.evidence: The use of Derivatives over unvested Company's Securities may allow value to be realised from those Securities even if performance hurdles have not been met. This would break the intended connection between staff performance and shareholder best interests.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities is expressly permitted rather than merely unaddressed, because 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' is a Derivative and section 7 permits Derivatives over vested Securities. Subject to Approved Trading Periods, prior approval or notice, the speculative trading ban and the 'front page' test.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, structured financial product or collar is within the definition of Derivatives and its entry is Trading (an agreement to sell or grant an option), so it is permitted over vested Securities but only in an Approved Trading Period with prior approval. Note that a short-dated forward risks being caught by the speculative trading ban, which names forward contracts as short term Trading.
rules.evidence: Trading means taking part in any transaction associated with applying for, buying, acquiring, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting, assigning rights to buy, sell or subscribe for, or agreeing to do any of these things

rules.detail: Any monetisation of unvested Equity Interests would be effected through a Derivative (forward, structured financial product, collar or 'any other hedging or investment arrangement') and is therefore banned outright.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Outright ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons. The policy defines short selling narrowly as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back lower, so a covered collar over shares actually held is not short selling on the policy's own definition.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Section 10 is directed only at Designated Personnel; Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel are not covered by an express short selling ban.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the definition of Trading. Borrowing securities is mentioned only descriptively in explaining what short selling is.

Contracts for difference and spread bets are expressly named as Derivatives. They are permitted in principle over vested Securities under section 7, but in practice a CFD over Company Securities is short term Trading caught by the speculative trading ban and, if short, by the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in speculative Trading in the Company's securities, such as Trading on considerations of a short term nature.

rules.detail: Flat ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons entering margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company Securities, with no vesting-state qualification, no approval route and no exemption. The phrase 'any margin lending arrangements' is broad enough to capture a bank loan margined against, and secured on, the collared shares.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons; the policy says nothing about margin lending by other Company Personnel.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not mentioned, and the definition of Trading covers buying, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting and assigning rights but not the creation of a security interest. There is no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.

The only financing prohibition is section 8, confined to 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements'. There is no general ban on secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, and no rule on what happens if a lender forces a sale. Whether a funded collar loan is caught turns on whether it is characterised as a margin lending arrangement.

Speculative Trading is banned, defined to include buying and selling Securities within a six month period and entering into other short term Trading, with forward contracts given as the example. Sale of shares received on vesting of employee incentives is carved out. This makes instrument tenor material: a collar maturing inside six months, or one written as a short-dated forward, is exposed to this prohibition.
rules.evidence: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).

rules.detail: Section 9 applies only to Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons.

ALQ.exemption_authority: Chair, at complete discretion, may grant prior written clearance to sell outside an Approved Trading Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or overriding legal requirement, or a pressing financial commitment); if the Chair is the applicant, the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee decides. The clearance is valid for seven business days, can be withdrawn on a change of circumstances, lapses immediately on acquiring Inside Information, and clears a breach of the policy only, not the insider trading laws. It extends to selling only, not to entering derivatives or financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are expressly within the defined term with no venue limit, so section 7 governs the structure directly: banned over unvested securities, permitted over vested ones.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a rare affirmative permission for hedging vested shares, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are contemplated rather than merely unprohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to margin loans strictly so called; a bank facility secured on the collared shares with margin or top-up mechanics is likely an 'arrangement in respect of Company's Securities' and would need to be structured, and confirmed with the Company Secretary, to sit outside it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no prohibition on pledging, charging or otherwise encumbering Company Securities other than section 8 on margin loans, and no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A non-margin term loan secured on the collared shares is not caught by any express prohibition, which is the key point of difference from policies that ban all secured financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar tenor should comfortably exceed six months and should not be documented as a forward, or it risks being characterised as speculative short term Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel ... are prohibited from Trading ... outside of the following periods: a period of one month commencing on the business day after the day full year results are announced; ... half year results ...; ... the Company's annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and any physical settlement of the collar must each fall inside one of only three one-month windows a year, and there is no exceptional-circumstances relief for anything other than a sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is silent on sales effected by a third party such as a lender, on margin calls and on price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither excused nor declared a breach: lender enforcement or cash-settlement outside a window is unregulated by the text but would sit uneasily with the window regime, so the facility should avoid discretionary lender sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances surrounding the Company, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Company Personnel or their Connected Persons taking advantage of their position in an inappropriate way? ... Any Trade in Company Securities ... must not be made if that Trade would fail the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-textured veto that sits above the express permissions, so the Chair or Managing Director can decline a collar on reputational grounds even where every specific rule is satisfied.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also applies to the Connected Persons of the Company Personnel ... or a company, trust or entity that the person or any of their Connected Persons controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the margin lending ban, the trading windows or the notice requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It is recognised that in exceptional circumstances, a Designated Personnel or their Connected Persons may need to sell the Company's Securities outside of an Approved Trading Period. ... A clearance is valid for seven business days from the date of the notification and can be withdrawn if there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only out-of-window relief is for a sale, so an urgent collar unwind or restructure outside a window has no sanctioned route.

ALQ.summary: A funded collar is possible for an ALS director or executive over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating on the derivative legs. Section 7 expressly permits the use of Derivatives, a term that names 'caps and collars' and 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' without venue limitation, in relation to vested Company Securities, while banning them outright over unvested equity incentives. The constraints are procedural and timing-based: Designated Personnel may only Trade in one of three one-month Approved Trading Periods following full year results, half year results and the AGM, a director must first inform the Chair and other Designated Personnel must obtain approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, written confirmation goes to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, and the tenor must exceed six months to avoid the speculative trading ban on buying and selling within six months and on forward contracts. The loan leg is the live issue: there is no general prohibition on secured financing or on encumbering shares, but section 8 bans Designated Personnel from 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities', so the facility must be a fixed term loan without margin or top-up mechanics and should be confirmed in advance with the Company Secretary. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or lender enforcement, so any lender sale right should be exercisable only within an Approved Trading Period, and the Chair's exceptional-circumstances discretion covers sales only and would not authorise an out-of-window unwind.

tiers.name: Team Members
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of The Lottery Corporation and its controlled entities, and all contractors, consultants, secondees and other personnel required to comply with its policies. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, company-imposed trading notices and, where they participate in an equity or incentive plan, the hedging and derivative ban over restricted and unvested awards; not subject to Blackout Periods or pre-clearance.

tiers.description: Directors of The Lottery Corporation. Must obtain written pre-clearance from the Chairman (the Chairman applies to the Chairman of the Audit Committee) before Trading at any time, are barred from Trading in Blackout Periods, from Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending and granting lenders any rights over their Securities, and must notify the Company Secretary of changes in notifiable interests within two business days.

No obligation to give reasons; a refusal or withdrawal of pre-clearance must be kept confidential by the applicant.

an acquisition of Securities pursuant to an offer made to all eligible holders of Securities of the same class (for example, a bonus issue, rights issue or buy-back);
an allocation of Securities under a share purchase plan or dividend reinvestment plan provided the participant did not commence or amend their participation in the plan during a Blackout Period
an acquisition of Securities under a Director, executive or employee equity or incentive plan;
a disposal of Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;
Trading that results in no change in the underlying beneficial interest in the Securities (for example, transfer from one personal shareholding to another personal shareholding);
investments by a fund or other scheme (such as an independent superannuation fund) where the investment decision is at the discretion of a third party.

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes. The Policy is to be read with the Non-Executive Director Shareholding Policy and the Executive Shareholding Policy, and pre-clearance may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy. The policy does not say whether hedged or encumbered shares are excluded from the count.
