TLC.exemption_authority: MD & CEO, or the Chairman in the case of Directors, may grant pre-clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Blackout Period or on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a pressing financial commitment, court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement) where the Trading is the only reasonable course of action available. The relief runs to sales and disposals only; there is no power to waive the hedging, margin lending or security interest prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: grant of any rights to lenders
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any The Lottery Corporation Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The second limb is a flat ban on giving a financier any rights over the shares, which defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar regardless of vesting state, loan purpose or loan-to-value ratio.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees, Directors and their Associates are prohibited from engaging in Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending, and from granting any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Key Principles restate the ban without even the word 'lenders', so on the policy's own summary a written call option granted over the shares to the bank is at risk of being read as a prohibited grant of rights, not merely the security interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Security Trading covered by this Policy includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every element of a funded collar, the put, the call, the charge and the loan, is separately a Trade requiring written pre-clearance and falling outside Blackout Periods, so there is no argument that only the share sale is regulated.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restricted shares included in hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights; and entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only shares that are both vested and free of plan restrictions can be collared, so the collar pool must be carefully identified against the plan records.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Trading that is the subject of pre-clearance must be executed within three business days of the receipt of the written pre-clearance (unless the pre-clearance is withdrawn).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The whole structure would have to be priced, documented and executed inside three business days of clearance, and the clearance can be withdrawn in the meantime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any pre-clearance to Trade can be given, withdrawn, refused or made subject to conditions by the applicable approver in their absolute discretion and without giving reasons. If pre-clearance is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the pre-clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on obtaining or keeping clearance, and the executive may be barred from explaining to the bank why a trade cannot proceed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An application for pre-clearance to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the derivative legs can be refused if the collar would leave the director or executive short of the minimum shareholding, so the collared parcel should sit above that requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Continuous Disclosure Committee may also, from time to time without prior notice, and conditionally or unconditionally, extend, reduce, or create an additional Blackout Period. ... The Board or Chairman may also, from time to time, at their absolute discretion, and without prior notice, impose ad hoc restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the executive bears that timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term Trading (Trading within six months of the acquisition) of The Lottery Corporation Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind must sit beyond six months from the acquisition of the underlying shares, or fall within the narrow exceptional circumstances relief.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates means any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with The Lottery Corporation or any of its Directors or Team Members (such as spouses, partners, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, joint venture partners).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family trust, family company or self-managed superannuation fund does not escape the security interest ban or the pre-clearance regime.

TLC.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a Lottery Corporation Director or Restricted Employee. The derivative legs alone would be workable over vested, unrestricted shares: the hedging and derivatives ban is confined to restricted shares and unvested performance options and rights, Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps and hedges whether cash settled or not, and creating a hedge is simply Trading that requires written pre-clearance from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (Restricted Employees), executed within three business days, outside the 1 January, 1 July and 1 October Blackout Periods and any additional blackout imposed by the Continuous Disclosure Committee. The loan leg fails: Directors and Restricted Employees and their Associates must not 'grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities', an unqualified prohibition with no vesting-state limit, no threshold and no waiver power, and the Key Principles state it even more broadly as a ban on 'granting any rights over' their Securities. The exceptional circumstances discretion extends only to selling or disposing of Securities in hardship or under legal compulsion, so it cannot be used to authorise a secured facility. Any structure would therefore have to be unsecured and cash settled, sit beyond six months from acquisition to avoid the Short-term Trading ban, and leave the executive compliant with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy, since pre-clearance may be refused on that ground.

tiers.name: ASX People

ASX.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The ASX Board determines ASX Trading Windows from time to time, may decline to open a Trading Window at any of the three ordinary times, and may elect to shorten, change or close a Trading Window at any time. In addition, pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, expressly including 'matters known to ASX, but not to you', so a confidential prohibition can be applied at the individual level.

rules.section: 2.5 (Derivatives and hedging arrangements over ASX Group Securities)
rules.detail: Absolute ban on any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities, with no venue limit and no approval route. A collar is squarely a transaction that limits economic risk.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The ban expressly extends to vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock, so the collar pool must be limited to vested shares free of any holding lock.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked ASX Group Securities is expressly contemplated rather than prohibited. The only stated requirement for directors is notification to the Company Secretary, and the position may be publicly disclosed. Pre-clearance under section 2.2 is expressed to apply to dealing in Covered Securities, which are financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, so an over-the-counter hedge is not itself a Covered Security, but the Policy requires compliance with its spirit as well as its letter.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.

rules.detail: Same position as directors: permitted over vested unlocked securities, subject to notifying the Company Secretary and possible public disclosure. No deadline or form is specified for the notification.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: A put, call or collar over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities limits economic risk and is caught by the express prohibition, whatever the venue.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and derivatives quoted on an Australian financial market are Covered Securities, so dealing in them requires pre-clearance through the online form, must be executed within five business days, and, where they are over ASX Group Securities, only in a designated ASX Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, debentures and hybrids, warrants, futures, options, derivatives and single-entity Exchange Traded Products (ETPs) ... You must not deal in Covered Securities without ASX pre-clearance approval.

rules.detail: An over-the-counter put or call is not quoted on an Australian financial market and so is not a Covered Security or a Security as defined, meaning the pre-clearance machinery does not by its terms bite on the derivative itself. What the Policy does require is notification to the Company Secretary of a derivative position over vested ASX Group Securities.
rules.evidence: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market.

rules.tier: NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees
rules.detail: These directors may not hold ASX Group securities at all and must divest any held on appointment, so there is no shareholding over which a collar could be written.
rules.evidence: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited (with any directors who hold ASX Group Securities prior to their appointment being required to divest those shares promptly and compliantly with this Policy).

rules.section: 2.5 (ASX Group Securities margin loans and other financing arrangements)
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Any monetisation that advances cash against the shares is a financing arrangement, and using ASX Group Securities as collateral for it is prohibited outright. An unsecured cash-settled monetisation would instead be treated as a hedging or derivative position requiring notification by executives and directors.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the three-month purchase-then-sale prohibition and by the requirement to pre-clear dealing in Covered Securities.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of Deal, which is confined to buying, acquiring, selling, transferring, disposing or converting Covered Securities or agreeing to do so.

Contracts for difference are not named. They are not quoted on an Australian financial market and so are not Covered Securities, but a CFD over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities would be caught by the ban on transactions limiting economic risk.

Flat ban on using ASX Group Securities as collateral for a new margin loan, with an added obligation to ensure that any portfolio of Covered Securities given as collateral contains no ASX Group Securities. Margin loans and financing over non-ASX Group Securities do not even require pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: Pledging or charging ASX Group Securities to any financier is prohibited because it is the use of those securities as collateral. The prohibition is framed by reference to entering a new margin loan or financing arrangement, so an encumbrance unconnected with financing is not expressly addressed, and creating a security interest is not itself within the definition of Deal.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans; it reaches any 'other financing arrangement' collateralised by ASX Group Securities, applies to all ASX people and their Connected Persons and to all vesting states, and applies to new arrangements. There is no approval route, although the section 2.8 waiver power is expressed to cover the Policy's dealing prohibitions generally.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: No purchase then sale, or sale then purchase, of Covered Securities of the same entity within three months. Market volatility is expressly rejected as a ground for exemption, and dealing that ASX considers frequent may also be denied clearance.
rules.evidence: You must not purchase then sell (and inversely sell and then purchase) any Covered Securities of the same entity within a three-month period. Market volatility will not be considered as a reason for exemption from this prohibition

rules.tier: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
rules.detail: Restated for NEDs in relation to ASX Group Securities specifically.
rules.evidence: Short-term dealing (that is, within a three-month period) in ASX Group Securities is prohibited.

ASX.exemption_authority: Waivers from the Policy's dealing prohibitions may be granted in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, a transfer under a family law property settlement, a testamentary disposition) where the proposed dealing is the only reasonable course of action available and the applicant holds no Inside Information; waivers may be conditional. bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar outright, including the technique of pledging a diversified portfolio that happens to contain ASX shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financing terms must not allow out-of-window sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the terms of your margin loan or financing arrangement does not require, nor allow for, ASX Group Securities to be disposed of at such time that would breach this Policy, such as outside of a designated ASX Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a lawful financing arrangement must be documented so that the lender has no right to sell ASX shares outside a Trading Window, which rules out ordinary bank enforcement and margin-call mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging vested shares is permitted but disclosable
bespoke_clauses.clause: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares is permitted, but the executive must accept notification and possible public disclosure of the position.

bespoke_clauses.topic: holding lock extends the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough; any holding lock on the shares must have lifted before they can be included in the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC instruments fall outside Covered Securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market. Covered Securities: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, options, derivatives, warrants, futures debentures, hybrids and single-entity ETPs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An over-the-counter put or call is not a Covered Security, so the pre-clearance and Trading Window machinery does not by its terms apply to the derivative legs, only the express hedging rule and the notification obligation do, but the 'letter and spirit' clause makes it prudent to pre-clear anyway.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may request a waiver from this Policy's dealing prohibitions in certain exceptional circumstances, including: severe financial hardship ... The proposed dealing is to be the only reasonable course of action available to you and any granted waiver may be subject to conditions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a secured facility, but it is limited to exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, so it cannot support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The ASX Board may decline to open a Trading Window during the periods listed above. The ASX Board may also elect to shorten, change or close a ASX Trading Window at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no guaranteed window, so any collar entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, including, but not limited, to: ... matters known to ASX, but not to you, and your ASX authorisation officer determines pre-clearance should not be granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the executive being able to trade at any particular time, and no reason for a refusal need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy contains a set of principles. You must comply with both the letter and spirit of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A structure engineered around the definition of Covered Securities to escape pre-clearance is exposed to challenge on spirit grounds even if the literal wording permits it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: CS licensee directors cannot hold at all
bespoke_clauses.clause: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For that group there is no underlying shareholding at all, so no collar, funded or otherwise, is possible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Persons are ASX peoples' spouse, de facto partner, children residing with the ASX person, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) or other entities controlled by an ASX person and/or their Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares in a family trust, company or SMSF does not avoid the collateral ban or the pre-clearance and window regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must deal within five business days once ASX pre-clearance approval has been granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared leg must be executed within five business days, which is workable for a negotiated OTC trade but leaves no room for extended documentation.

ASX.summary: A funded collar is not possible for an ASX Limited director or executive, although the derivative legs alone are. Section 2.5 expressly permits transactions limiting economic risk over vested ASX Group Securities that are not subject to a holding lock, banning them only over unvested or holding-locked securities, and the only formality for ASX Group Executives and Directors is notification to the Company Secretary, with possible public disclosure; the OTC legs are not themselves Covered Securities, though the Policy's 'letter and spirit' clause makes pre-clearance prudent and any exchange-traded leg would require it, be executable only within five business days and confined to a Trading Window opened at the ASX Board's discretion after half-year results, full-year results and the AGM. The loan leg fails outright: ASX people are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement, and must ensure that any collateral portfolio contains no ASX Group Securities. The Policy goes further and requires that the terms of any financing arrangement neither require nor allow ASX Group Securities to be disposed of outside a Trading Window, which would rule out conventional lender enforcement and margin-call rights even if collateral were permitted. The only conceivable route is a section 2.8 waiver from Enterprise Risk and Compliance or the Chair for severe financial hardship where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, which will not support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar, and Non-Executive Directors of the Clearing & Settlement facility licensees may not hold ASX Group securities at all.

TNE.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the CEO may impose additional blackout periods as necessary. The policy does not say whether they are announced or confidential, and gives no criteria or duration.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. Securities expressly include derivatives and Trading includes 'otherwise dealing in' them, so a put or call over TechnologyOne shares is Trading: it needs the Chair's prior approval, must fall in a Trading Window, must not be done while holding Inside Information, and must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days. bespoke_clauses.clause: Covered Persons are prohibited from: ... Using TechnologyOne's Securities as security for loans or margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, employee and contractor, with no approval or waiver route, so the funded structure cannot be offered.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked stock
bespoke_clauses.clause: Covered Persons are not permitted at any time to enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge their exposure to TechnologyOne securities which have not vested or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the loan ban, the hedging prohibition stops at unvested and locked shares, so an unfunded collar over vested unrestricted shares is not itself prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Securities" include shares, options, derivatives, and any other financial products of TechnologyOne that can be traded on a financial market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading (buying and selling Securities within a 3-month period).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities expressly include derivatives, buying a put and writing a call and then unwinding either leg inside three months risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading, so the collar tenor and any roll should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional blackout periods may be imposed by the Board or CEO as necessary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board or CEO can close the trading window without notice or stated criteria, so pricing, unwind or physical settlement of a collar can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all directors, officers, employees, and contractors of TechnologyOne and its subsidiaries (referred to as "Covered Persons").
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy never extends to spouses, dependants or controlled entities and trusts, so its literal reach over shares held through a family trust is untested rather than clearly prohibited; the bank should not treat that as a workaround.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Details of Trading in TechnologyOne Securities undertaken by the Chair, Directors or KMP are to be provided to the Company Secretary as soon as possible and within two business days of the Trade at the latest so that notification can be made via the ASX Announcements Platform.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll and unwind by a Director or KMP will be disclosed publicly through Appendix 3Y-style notification within two business days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chair, Directors and KMP are required to be granted approval from the following before Trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy states no validity period, response time, conditions power or revocation right for an approval, so the bank cannot rely on a defined execution window and should obtain the approval terms in writing before pricing.

TNE.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The derivative legs alone are workable over vested, unrestricted shares: the express hedging ban is confined to securities that have not vested or remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction, so a put and call over free shares is only 'Trading', requiring the Chair's prior approval for Directors and KMP (approval by the Audit & Risk Committee Chair and Managing Director for the Chair), execution in a Trading Window outside the 1 February, 1 March and 1 September blackouts, no Inside Information, and notification to the Company Secretary within two business days for ASX release. The loan leg is fatal: section 9 flatly prohibits every Covered Person from using TechnologyOne Securities as security for loans or margin lending, with no approval, tier or vesting carve-out, and the only exemption power (severe hardship or a court order) reaches blackout-period trading only. Because Securities expressly include derivatives, tenor and any roll or unwind should exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, and the Board or CEO can impose additional blackouts at any time. An unfunded collar is therefore available with clearance, but the bank cannot take security over the shares.

ORI.title: Policy: Securities Dealing

tiers.name: Directors, employees and contractors
tiers.description: The general population to whom the policy applies. They may deal freely unless they hold inside information, have been formally notified that they are restricted, or are a Restricted Person. No blackout periods, no approval requirement and none of the 'prohibited dealings' (margin loans, hedging, short-term dealing, short selling) apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any Director of Orica Limited, executives who are members of the Executive Committee, and any other employee who has regular access to inside information or has been advised by Company Secretariat that they are subject to the additional dealing restrictions. tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, your dealings in Securities (including spouse or partner and their child or dependant), or a company or other entity which you have an ability to control or significantly influence. ORI.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may specify 'any other period' as a blackout period for Restricted Persons, and may also formally notify any individual (Restricted Person or not) that they are restricted from dealing. rules.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings; Glossary (Deal or dealing, Securities)
rules.detail: Securities expressly include 'any other financial product relating to securities whether or not the product is created by Orica or by a third party', and dealing includes 'entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations', so an OTC put or call over Orica shares is a dealing in Securities. Because the put and call legs of a collar are hedging, they fall squarely within the express prohibited dealings list for Restricted Persons. A non-hedging derivative would instead require written approval and fall outside blackout periods.

rules.section: General Dealing Restrictions; Glossary (Deal or dealing, Securities)
rules.detail: For employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons the prohibited dealings list does not apply. A derivative over Orica Securities is a dealing, so it is barred only while the person holds inside information or has been formally notified that they are restricted; no approval, blackout or notification applies. Employees are told to consider perception issues and consult the Company Secretary if necessary.

rules.detail: Hedging is listed as a flatly prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons. rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging;

rules.section: General Dealing Restrictions; Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressed only as an 'additional dealing restriction' applying to Restricted Persons, so employees and contractors outside that tier are not prohibited from hedging; the only constraints are inside information, a formal restriction notice, and the general perception warning.

rules.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings; Glossary (Deal or dealing)
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan is an arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations and is therefore a dealing; in substance it is hedging, which is prohibited for Restricted Persons, and if funded by a loan against the shares it also engages the margin loan prohibition.

ORI.exemption_authority: Only the 'exceptional circumstances' power, which permits a Restricted Person to deal during a blackout period with written approval from the Chairman (Directors), the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee (Chairman), the Company Secretary (any other Restricted Person) or the Managing Director & CEO (Company Secretary), on grounds such as demonstrated and severe financial hardship. There is no power to waive the prohibited dealings list (margin loans, hedging, short-term dealing, short selling).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging; - short-term dealing, including buying and selling Securities on market within a three month period; and - short selling.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Hedging' is undefined and unlimited by vesting state or venue, so a collar over fully vested unrestricted shares is prohibited for every Director and Executive Committee member, with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing prohibition names only margin loans rather than secured financing generally, so the loan leg is not expressly banned; but with the hedge itself prohibited the point is academic, and a loan advanced against collared shares may still be characterised as a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities Includes, in relation to Orica Limited: ... any other financial product relating to securities whether or not the product is created by Orica or by a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call are expressly Securities, so every leg of a collar and every roll or unwind is a dealing subject to the policy rather than sitting outside it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: profit or loss arrangements are dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or dealing Includes: ... entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This limb catches economically synthetic structures (collars, CFDs, prepaid forwards) even when no share changes hands, so no cash-settled variant escapes the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Do not deal in Securities if the Company has formally notified you that you are restricted from dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an employee outside the Restricted Persons tier can be individually blocked at any time without notice or criteria, so a counterparty cannot rely on a person's tier remaining unrestricted for the life of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to deal may be withdrawn at any time if there is a change in circumstance, and any decision to refuse approval is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be pulled after it is given and before execution, and the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so there is execution risk between pricing and signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person approved to deal must deal no later than two business days commencing on the day after approval is received, otherwise new approval must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside a two business day window, which is tight for negotiating and signing OTC derivative and loan documentation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of Directors, employees and contractors are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that individual. ... a company or any other entity which you have an ability to control or significantly influence.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedging prohibition, and the Restricted Person must obtain written approval for dealings on the associate's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.topic: plan shares remain in scope after release
bespoke_clauses.clause: Applying for or acquiring Securities under an employee incentive scheme; however, for clarity, any subsequent dealing of Securities which cease to be held under the terms of a scheme remains subject to the provisions of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares released from an incentive plan do not become policy-free, so vested shares held by a Restricted Person remain subject to the hedging prohibition.

ORI.summary: A funded collar is not available to Orica Directors or Executive Committee members. They are Restricted Persons, and the policy flatly prohibits 'hedging' in respect of Securities with no definition, no vesting distinction, no venue limit, no approval route and no exceptional-circumstances relief, so the purchased put and written call are barred over vested unrestricted shares as much as over unvested ones. The financing leg is drafted more narrowly, catching only 'margin loans' rather than secured financing generally, so a bank loan secured on the shares is not expressly named, but that does not rescue the structure and such a loan may itself be characterised as a margin loan. Employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons are not subject to the prohibited dealings list and could in principle hedge, but they would rarely be the intended clients and can be made subject to a formal restriction notice at any time. If Orica were ever to permit a structure, it would still need written approval valid for only two business days, would have to avoid the 1 April and 1 October blackouts, would be disclosed by Directors to the Company Secretary within two business days, and would have to exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban.

ALD.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Caltex staff
tiers.description: Directors, full-time, part-time and casual employees, consultants, secondees, contractors of, and persons seconded to, the Caltex Group. Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade at any time provided they hold no inside information; none of the closed periods, clearance requirements or trading restrictions (derivatives, short-term, short selling, hedging, margin lending and secured financing) apply to them.

This tier carries the closed periods, the trading clearance regime, the post-trade notification duty and all of the substantive trading restrictions. The only differentiation within the tier is the identity of the clearance approver.

tiers.description: Immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries. ALD.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Caltex Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it must be advised to the Designated Caltex Personnel, so it is notified to those affected but not necessarily announced to the market. rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives; Definitions
rules.detail: The policy expressly extends to derivative markets and derivative products, naming warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, over both vested securities and unvested entitlements, and Caltex securities are defined to include third-party issued options and swaps. A derivative is therefore a trade requiring clearance, outside closed periods, with post-trade notification. This does not rescue collar legs: any derivative that limits risk exposure is separately prohibited by the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel are outside the closed periods, the clearance regime and the Trading Restrictions section, so a derivative over Caltex securities is limited only by the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.detail: An effects-based ban on any arrangement limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities, expressly extended to vested securities. There is no approval route, no de minimis and no venue limit; the exceptional circumstances discretion relieves only against the closed period prohibition, not against this restriction.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.detail: The same ban expressly reaches unvested entitlements under Caltex employee incentive schemes, so unvested rights cannot be hedged or used as the reference asset for a derivative.
rules.evidence: including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Insider Trading Prohibition
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressed to bind Designated Caltex Personnel only, so staff outside that tier are not prohibited from hedging; the insider trading prohibition still applies at all times.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each has the effect of limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities and so falls within the hedging ban, and if the advance is secured on the shares it is separately caught by the secured financing prohibition.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities

rules.detail: Flat ban on entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities, with no approval route or security-state carve-out. The reference to 'any arrangements' would reach synthetic short exposure as well as physical short sales.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. A stock loan transfers the legal interest in the security and is therefore a 'trade', so it would need clearance, fall outside closed periods and be notified within three days; it is not separately prohibited unless it forms part of a short selling or risk-limiting arrangement.
rules.evidence: "trade" includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in a security.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives, Short-term Trading, Short Selling, Hedging Transactions
rules.detail: Contracts for differences are expressly brought within the policy, so they are trades requiring clearance rather than being outside it. In practice most CFD positions are separately prohibited: a short CFD by the short selling ban, a risk-limiting CFD by the hedging ban, and any CFD closed out within six months by the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences)

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Margin lending in respect of Caltex securities is expressly prohibited at all times for all Designated Caltex Personnel, with no approval route, no vesting carve-out and no grandfathering.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Granting security over Caltex securities to support financing is prohibited as a secured financing arrangement. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named, and the definition of 'trade' does not expressly sweep in the creation of a security interest.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: The prohibition is deliberately wider than margin loans, extending to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. It binds every Director and CLT member regardless of security state, has no clearance or waiver route, and the exceptional circumstances discretion is confined to closed period trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Six month ban on short-term or speculative trading, expressly extended to derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, with purchase and sale of the same securities within six months given as an inclusive example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for all Designated Caltex Personnel except Directors; Chairman of the Board for Directors (excluding the Chairman); Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board. Requests go by email to secretariat@caltex.com.au and the Company Secretary follows an Internal Approval Process before confirming.
clearance.post_trade_to: Caltex Secretariat (contract note, or an email with holder name, SRN/HIN, number or dollar value, price, date and nature of trade); Directors should also notify the Company Secretary as soon as practical after any Permitted Trading
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than three days after the date of the trade
clearance.evidence: Clearance for trading in Caltex securities is only valid for trading notified in the request for clearance and will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted. ... The Caltex Secretariat will respond to requests for clearance to trade in Caltex securities within one business day of receipt of the request.
Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

clearance.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading by Connected Persons
clearance.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel must take reasonable steps, including notifying their closely connected persons of closed periods, to prevent any closely connected persons from trading in Caltex securities in any way that is prohibited under this policy.

short_term.basis: purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities, given as an inclusive example of short term or speculative trading; expressly extends to derivative products over Caltex securities
short_term.evidence: including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship if, in the opinion of the person exercising the discretion, they are only able to meet their financial commitments by selling their securities ... and the proposed disposal of Caltex securities is the only reasonable course of action to overcome these circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: exceptional personal circumstances;

acquisition of securities under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders in Caltex, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Caltex Board;
disposal of securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme or arrangement or equal access buy-back;
transfers of Caltex securities where there is no change in the person's underlying beneficial interest in the securities;
transfers of securities between someone closely related such as a spouse, minor child, family company or family trust or to their superannuation fund;

disposal by Designated Caltex Personnel of Caltex securities under a pre-determined divestment plan where the plan cannot be cancelled during a closed period (other than in exceptional circumstances) and: they entered into the plan outside a closed period; they have not amended the plan during a closed period; the plan does not permit them to exercise any discretion over how, when and whether to dispose of securities.

indirect or incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of Designated Caltex Personnel dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio securities in Caltex;

The restrictions on trading during closed periods do not apply to: offers made to Caltex staff to participate in Caltex short and long term incentive plans and share plans (together, Plans); acceptance by Caltex staff of offers referred to above ... and transfers of unrestricted Caltex securities from the Trustee of any of the Plans to Caltex staff

external_documents: Internal Approval Process followed by the Company Secretary before confirming clearance to trade
ALD.exemption_authority: The Chairman of the Board (for Directors and CLT) and the Chairman of the Audit Committee (for the Chairman of the Board) have a discretion to exempt from the closed period prohibition only, and only for severe financial hardship, exceptional personal circumstances, or to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement, where disposal is the only reasonable course of action. No person has authority to waive the hedging, short selling, short-term trading, margin lending or secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: effects-based hedging ban over vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is drafted by economic effect and expressly reaches vested shares, so the purchased put and written call of a collar are prohibited outright for every Director and CLT member with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing wider than margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited, so the funded element fails even before the hedging ban is considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no argument that a bilateral OTC collar sits outside the policy; it is expressly captured, over both vested and unvested exposure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Caltex securities" includes ordinary shares of Caltex and any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, option, warrant, or other derivative over an ordinary share of Caltex, whether issued by Caltex or a third party, and any other interest in an ordinary share of Caltex.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves Caltex securities, so the six month short-term trading ban and the closed period restrictions apply to the derivative legs and to any roll or unwind, not just to the underlying shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: six month short-term ban including derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if hedging were permitted, any collar with a tenor, roll or early unwind inside six months would be separately prohibited as short-term or speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance ... will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted ... Clearance to trade can be given or refused without giving any reasons and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. If clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be executed inside 14 calendar days, can be revoked between grant and execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a refusal occurred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance to trade may be withheld for perception reasons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant transaction can be blocked on reputational grounds alone, which is precisely the ground on which a director's collar would be scrutinised.

bespoke_clauses.topic: transfer to a third party holding is a trade
bespoke_clauses.clause: Nature of proposed trade (i.e. on market purchase, on-market transfer or sale, transfer to super fund).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance form treats a transfer to another holding vehicle as a notifiable trade, so moving collared shares into a bank custody or security account would require clearance and post-trade notification, even though transfers with no change in beneficial interest are listed as Permitted Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel must notify the Caltex Secretariat of details of any trading in Caltex securities by submitting a contract note to secretariat@caltex.com.au no later than three days after the date of the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar entry, roll or unwind by a Director or CLT member is reported to the Secretariat within three days and, for Directors, flows into ASX disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "closely connected persons" of Caltex staff include immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family company or trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: All of the collar-relevant prohibitions bind only Designated Caltex Personnel, but any employee can be notified into that tier at any time, so a counterparty cannot rely on a client remaining outside it for the life of the trade.

ALD.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Ampol (Caltex) Director or Leadership Team member. Both legs of the structure are separately and expressly prohibited: the hedging restriction bans 'any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities', and the financing restriction bans 'any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. Neither prohibition has an approval route, and the only discretion in the policy, exercisable by the Chairman of the Board or the Chairman of the Audit Committee, relieves solely against the closed period restriction on grounds of severe hardship, exceptional personal circumstances or a court order. The policy expressly captures over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, and defines third-party derivatives over Caltex shares as Caltex securities, so no cash-settled or offshore variant escapes it, and the six month short-term trading ban would independently bar a short-dated collar. Only Caltex staff outside the Designated Caltex Personnel tier fall outside these restrictions, and any employee can be notified into that tier at any time.
